full_description:
### Description
In General visibility mode = "When target is casting an interruptible spell", the icon grid and cast bar intermittently light up for **non-interruptible** casts that should stay hidden. Root cause (from a code trace): the interruptibility alpha-mask is purely event-driven with no polling. WoW frequently reports `UnitCastingInfo.notInterruptible` as **falsy at `UNIT_SPELLCAST_START`** and only corrects it via `UNIT_SPELLCAST_NOT_INTERRUPTIBLE`, which fires **only on a transition** — so a spell that is non-interruptible for its *entire* duration may never emit that event, leaving the grid + cast bar at alpha 1 for the whole cast.

Two gaps prevent self-correction:
- `modules/IconGrid.lua` `EnableUnit` (~L608-616) does **not** register `UNIT_SPELLCAST_DELAYED` / `UNIT_SPELLCAST_CHANNEL_UPDATE`, so a pushback never re-runs `RefreshVisibility` → `ApplyInterruptibilityMask`.
- `modules/Castbar.lua` `OnCastDelayed` (~L1324-1349) re-reads the corrected `notInterruptible` and re-colors child widgets but **never re-applies the frame-level `ApplyVisibilityMask`**, so the bar frame stays fully visible even though the corrected flag is already in hand.

### Steps to reproduce
1. General visibility = "When target is casting an interruptible spell"; frame **locked**.
2. In Murder Row, target the **Bribed Guard** NPC.
3. Watch it cast **Shield Bash** / **Crimson Glaive** (both non-interruptible).
4. Intermittently the grid + cast bar light up for these non-interruptible casts.

### Expected
Non-interruptible casts never show the grid/cast bar in this mode (alpha 0 for the whole cast).

### Actual
Intermittently they show at full alpha for the entire cast.

### Proposed fix (narrowest → most robust)
- Register `UNIT_SPELLCAST_DELAYED` + `UNIT_SPELLCAST_CHANNEL_UPDATE` on the grid (`OnUnitCastEvent` already re-masks via `RefreshVisibility`).
- Add `ApplyVisibilityMask(inst.frame, inst.unit)` to `Castbar:OnCastDelayed`.
- And/or a one-shot deferred re-apply (`C_Timer.After` after START/CHANNEL_START) to pick up the settled `notInterruptible` even when Blizzard never emits a change event.

All interruptibility handling must stay secret-value-safe (`notInterruptible` passed straight into `SetAlphaFromBoolean`, never compared in Lua) per `docs/midnight-quirks.md`.

### Not part of this bug (by design)
While the frame is **unlocked**, the interruptibility filter is intentionally bypassed (everything shows so you can drag). The default is now `locked=false`, so a fresh profile shows all casts until `/kcd lock`. Expected behavior, not this bug.

### Environment
KickCD 1.2.0 · Interface 120007 (WoW 12.0.7 Midnight)

full_description:
Deferred from the 2026-07-31 review (finding F-008), re-deferred by
/wow-addon:pending-audit as item PLAN-03.

## Evidence

> ### F-008 — the mirror refresher rebuilds off-screen panels `[perf][ux]`
> **Where:** `settings/UnitPanel.lua:463-471`.
> **Problem:** The registered refresher calls `Helpers.RenderUnitPanel(ctx, pageKey)` — a full
> `ClearScroll` + rebuild — whenever the unit's mirror state changed since the last render, with no
> `ctx.panel:IsShown()` check. options-ui-§11 requires structural rebuilds to be scoped to the
> on-screen subcategory, with off-screen panels flagged dirty for a lazy rebuild on next `OnShow`
> (anti-patterns #39).
> **Impact:** One `/at set units.focus.mirror true`, one Defaults click, or one profile switch tears
> down and rebuilds every rendered Bar/Border/Font panel, including the two the user cannot see.
> Three pages is not the ~15 that produced the half-second stall the rule was written from, so this
> is a latency and widget-churn concern rather than a visible freeze.
> **Direction:** Gate the re-render on `ctx.panel and ctx.panel:IsShown()`; otherwise set
> `ctx.__dirty = true` and extend each page's first-show guard to re-render when dirty. The in-place
> checkbox re-sync above it stays unconditional — that half is already compliant.

## Location

`settings/UnitPanel.lua:463-471`, plus the first-show guards in `settings/Bar.lua`,
`settings/Border.lua` and `settings/Font.lua`.

## Severity

Medium — a deviation from the Ka0s WoW Addon Standard (options-ui-§11, anti-patterns #39) carried
over from a review bundle. Not a correctness bug: the behaviour predates the LibKa0s extraction and
was carried verbatim from the deleted `settings/Helpers.lua`.

## Why it is still open

Deferred in commit `ef71076` to protect the M9 in-game pass, whose purpose was confirming the
extraction changed nothing visible. It is now the addon's only remaining structural rebuild —
everything else refreshes in place inside LibKa0s.

## Design already specified

`docs/reviews/2026-07-31/02_PROPOSED_CHANGES.md` (C-7) and `04_EXECUTION_PLAN.md` (M3.2).

full_description:
## Summary

Containers can currently track `player`, `target`, `focus` and pet. Add the party unit tokens so a container can show a party member's buffs/debuffs. The requesting user asked for "Party #1-5"; in WoW the usable tokens are `party1`-`party4` (the fifth member is the player, already covered by `player`).

## Why it was deferred

Kept out of v0.1.0 by request, to ship the core feature set first.

## Design notes

- Each container is a Blizzard 12.1 `AuraContainer` (`CustomAuraContainerTemplate`) whose unit is set with `SetUnit`.
- Add `party1`-`party4` to `NS.Constants.UNITS` / `UNIT_LABELS` in `core/Constants.lua`.
- The engine does not notice when a token like `party1` starts pointing at a different person, so containers must be refreshed on `GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE` — mirror the existing `addon:OnUnitSwap` handler in `core/AuraMaster.lua`, which calls `UpdateAllAuras`.
- A container should hide or disable itself while its unit does not exist (e.g. not in a group, or a smaller group).
- Spell-id candidate filters are already honored for buffs on friendly units, so party buff containers can reuse the existing spell-list categories without new filtering logic.
- Consider a "one container per party member" convenience that clones a container across `party1`-`party4` and anchors them in a chain, to save manual setup.
- Update `docs/scope.md`, `docs/settings-panel.md`, and the README to document the new unit tokens.

## Acceptance

- A container set to `party1` shows that member's auras, both in and out of combat.
- Roster changes (people joining/leaving/reordering the party) refresh the container correctly.
- Headless tests cover the expanded unit list and the roster-refresh behavior.

full_description:
Found by the whole-branch review of feedback batch 6 (2026-09-15), and accepted for now by the owner.

## What happens

A category set to Show compiles to its own aura group (spec section 6b, `R-4`). So a container with
any category Hidden — or with "Only these categories" on — compiles to roughly one group per Show
category plus a catch-all, around 15 of them.

`lookOf` in `modules/FilterCompiler.lua` stamps the same `sortMethod` and `sortDirection` onto every
group, and the engine sorts WITHIN a group and lays the groups out by `layoutIndex`. So the auras
come out category-block by category-block, each block sorted internally — not as one flat sorted
list.

Concretely: set Sort by = Time remaining, hide Consumables on a buff container, and the bars are
grouped by category rather than ordered by time.

## Why it is not simply a bug

It follows from the priority model the owner chose: "an aura in at least one Show category is drawn,
even if another of its categories says Hide" is a union over heterogeneous predicates, and the
engine only ORs by using separate groups. There is no exact cheaper shape — two candidate
optimizations were analysed and rejected during the batch, both because they changed which auras
were drawn once a max-aura cap was set.

The same root cause makes the max-aura cap per group; that one is already documented on the setting.

## What was done instead

The Sort by and Direction descriptions now state the behavior plainly, matching the treatment the
max-aura row already got, and smoke check 77 gained an ordering clause so a tester verifies the
order rather than mere presence.

## What a fix would need

Revisiting rank 3 of the priority order, which is the thing that forces the groups. That reopens a
decision the owner made deliberately, so it is filed rather than acted on.

full_description:
Requested by the owner, 2026-09-15.

## What

Build an export string for a profile — and ideally for a single container — and accept an import
string back, the way EllesmereUI, ElvUI and WeakAuras2 do. Sharing a setup should not mean telling
someone which twenty settings to change by hand.

## Why it is not already there

`docs/scope.md` records this as a known gap: profiles persist in `AuraMasterDB` through AceDB and
there is **no serialization layer at all**. So this is new machinery, not a switch.

## What it would need

- **Serialize + deserialize.** The obvious route is the Ace stack already vendored (AceSerializer,
  plus a compressor and a base64 pass so the string survives the chat box). Check what is bundled
  before adding a dependency.
- **A version stamp inside the string**, checked on import against `Database.CurrentSchemaVersion()`.
  The stored shape is at schema v3 and has changed three times; an import from an older string must
  run the same migration ladder rather than writing a stale shape straight into the profile.
- **Scope choice on export** — a whole profile, or one container. Per-container is the more useful
  half in practice: "here is my debuff bar" is the thing people actually share.
- **A preview before it applies.** An import that silently replaces a profile is how people lose
  work. Show what is about to change, and make it cancellable.
- **Validation, not trust.** An import string is untrusted input: unknown keys dropped, values
  range-checked against the schema, spell ids sanity-checked. The schema already knows every path's
  type and range, so most of this can be driven off it rather than hand-written.

## Out of scope for the request

Sharing through anything but a string the player copies. No addon-to-addon channel, no website.

full_description:
### Description

Let a container anchor to a **nameplate**: the target's, the focus's or the pet's, and for the
player to the **Personal Resource Display**.

### Motivation

Aura Master already places a container on the screen, on another container, or on a named frame
(`modules/Anchors.lua`, `modules/FramePicker.lua`). The one placement it cannot express is the one
a target-debuff container most wants — *on the target's nameplate, above its health bar* — so a
player watching their own DoTs or CC on the target has to read them somewhere other than where they
are looking.

### This is not the same as the "nameplate units" scope entry

`docs/scope.md` → *Out of scope by decision* says: **"Raid, arena, boss and nameplate units.
Containers are for a handful of units the player watches, not a unit-frame replacement."**

That entry is about the container's **unit** — it declines `nameplate1`..`nameplateN` as unit
tokens, i.e. a container per visible enemy. This request is different and does not reopen it: the
container keeps its existing unit (`target`, `focus`, `pet`, `player`) and only changes **where it
is drawn**. One container, one unit, anchored to that unit's nameplate. If this ships, that scope
entry should be reworded so the distinction is explicit, rather than left to read as a refusal of
this too.

### Why the existing "frame" mode cannot do it

`attach.mode = "frame"` resolves a **static global frame name**, re-resolved when the addon owning
it loads (`defaults/Profile.lua`, the `attach` block; `modules/Anchors.lua:88-91`). Nameplate frames
do not work that way:

- They are created on demand and **recycled**. The frame showing your target is whichever
  `NamePlate<N>` the engine currently has bound to it, and that binding changes as units come and go
  — so a name saved in a profile points at the wrong unit minutes later.
- They appear and disappear constantly, including mid-combat, and the target changes independently
  of both.

So this needs a genuine anchor mode, not a new value for the existing one: resolve through
`C_NamePlate.GetNamePlateForUnit(unit)`, follow `NAME_PLATE_UNIT_ADDED` / `NAME_PLATE_UNIT_REMOVED`
plus the existing unit-swap events, and re-anchor (or hide) as the binding moves.

### Proposed behavior

- A new `attach.mode = "nameplate"`, which follows the container's **own** unit. No new unit tokens.
- `player` resolves to the Personal Resource Display, which is the player's own nameplate
  (`C_NamePlate.GetNamePlateForUnit("player")`).
- When the unit has no nameplate — out of range, nameplates disabled, the Personal Resource Display
  turned off, or the unit is dead or gone — the container hides rather than falling back to the
  screen, so it can never be left stranded at a stale position.
- The existing point / relative-point / offset controls apply unchanged.

### Open questions for design

- **Combat.** Anchoring our own (unprotected) frame to a nameplate should be legal under lockdown,
  unlike the Blizzard-frame reparenting the addon already defers (`docs/scope.md`, and
  `modules/BlizzardFrames.lua`). This needs confirming rather than assuming — a re-anchor that turns
  out to be blocked mid-combat is the whole feature failing exactly when it is being watched.
- **Personal Resource Display** is off by default and is toggled by a CVar
  (`nameplateShowSelf`). Decide whether the addon detects and explains that, or silently hides.
- **Scale.** Nameplates carry their own scale, which the container's own sizing does not know about.
- **Which sub-frame** to anchor to: the nameplate's health bar, or the whole plate.
- Interaction with `modules/Preview.lua` test mode, which has no nameplate to hang from.
- Whether a container attached to a nameplate-anchored container (`Anchors.Followers`) behaves.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A container can anchor to its unit's nameplate for `target`, `focus` and `pet`.
- [ ] A `player` container can anchor to the Personal Resource Display.
- [ ] The anchor follows nameplate add / remove and unit swaps, and hides when there is none.
- [ ] Combat behavior is established and documented, not assumed.
- [ ] `docs/scope.md`'s nameplate entry is reworded to separate nameplate **units** (still declined)
      from nameplate **anchoring** (this).
- [ ] Test-mode behavior is defined.

### Related

- #1 — party units, the other placement/unit widening.

full_description:
Moving an item straight from the character bank to a warband tab is not recorded today.

**Why.** Capture pairs a movement by requiring that *both* sides change, and the bags must be one of those two sides. A store-to-store move changes neither bag count, so nothing pairs and the movement is invisible. This is documented under *Known limitations* in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.

**What it would take.** A second pairing rule that matches two stores against each other, rather than a store against the bags.

**The hard part.** The bags-must-move rule is the invariant that keeps phantom rows out — F-001 in the 2026-07-27 review cycle was exactly that failure mode, where a bank-tab purchase was recorded as a warband gold deposit. A store-vs-store rule needs to answer:

- how it avoids double-counting a movement the existing bags rule already paired;
- what it does when three or more containers change in a single pass;
- which smoke tests prove it does not invent rows.

Design pass first, then code. Deferred via `/wow-addon:pending-audit` on 2026-07-31 (item `DOC-03`).

full_description:
A ledger row written while the client had not yet cached the item keeps only its item id, permanently. Such a row shows as `Item <id>` in History and drops out of the Type, Sub-type and Quality breakdowns in Insights for good. Documented under *Known limitations* in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.

**The pieces already exist.** `Compat.ItemNameQuality` returns `(name, quality)` and is nil-safe for an uncached id, and `Compat` already has a request-and-callback path that fires once an id loads (`core/Compat.lua:215-225`). The settings Filters list uses exactly this — `settings/Panel.lua:467` notes that a background load is kicked off so a later rebuild fills the name in. Stored ledger rows never get the same treatment.

**What it would take.** Walk stored history for rows missing `itemName`, request those ids, and rewrite the rows as they resolve.

**The care needed.** This is a write path over the saved variables, so it wants:

- a bound on how much it walks and requests at login, so it cannot stall the client;
- idempotency, so a repeated run cannot corrupt or duplicate a row;
- a decision on whether it also backfills `quality`, `itemType` and `itemSubType` — which is what actually returns the row to the Insights breakdowns.

Deferred via `/wow-addon:pending-audit` on 2026-07-31 (item `DOC-04`).

full_description:
### Description
Some consumables can only be used in specific zones or instances — e.g. Potato Stew
Feast and Feast of Ribs. ConsumableMaster currently ranks and selects purely on what
is in bags, so a zone-locked item can win a category and produce a macro that errors
out when used elsewhere.

### Motivation
A macro that fails on use is worse than one offering a lower-ranked item: the player
finds out mid-pull. Zone awareness keeps the selected item actually castable.

### Proposed behavior
- Mark zone-restricted items in the defaults data with their usability constraint.
- Have the Selector/Ranker skip items whose restriction is not currently satisfied,
  falling through to the next-best candidate.
- Re-evaluate on zone change so the macro updates when entering/leaving a valid zone.
- The exact detection mechanism (tooltip-scraped restriction text vs. a maintained
  item list vs. an API check) is _TBD_ — needs investigation.

### Acceptance criteria
- A zone-locked item is not selected while outside its valid zone, even if it would
  otherwise outrank everything in bags.
- Entering a valid zone makes the item eligible again without a `/reload`.
- Full list of affected items identified and captured in the defaults data.
- Tests + `luacheck` stay green.

full_description:
### Context

Three of this addon's LibKa0s Slash locale overrides — `ERR_BOOL`, `ERR_ALLOWED` and `ERR_COLOR` — have never taken effect, because the library functions that emit them read `lib.STRINGS` directly rather than through the instance resolver. The fix belongs upstream in LibKa0s, not in the vendored copy.

### Evidence

Source: `libs/LibKa0s/Slash.lua` — three `L` keys the descriptor cannot reach

Evidence hash: `errstrings-upstream`

### Deferral rationale

`ERR_BOOL`, `ERR_ALLOWED` and `ERR_COLOR` are emitted by `parseBool`, `allowedText` and `parseColor`, which sit ABOVE `lib:New` and therefore read `lib.STRINGS` directly rather than through `Sl:Text`. An instance `L` override cannot reach them, so this addon's three overrides — declared since the adoption, and each pinning wording it had already shipped — have never taken effect: a bad boolean answers the library's "expected true/false/on/off/1/0/yes/no" and a bad enum answers "allowed values:" in lowercase. Nothing is broken, and the four keys that DO route through `Sl:Text` work. Deferred rather than closed because the fix belongs upstream (hoist the parsers onto the instance, or thread the resolver into them) and `libs/` is not this repo's to edit. The three keys stay in `SLASH_STRINGS` as the record of the intended wording, marked dead in place. `tests/test_slashsetup.lua`'s enum case lowercases before matching, which is why it never noticed.

### Provenance

Migrated from `docs/pending/LEDGER.md` row `LIBKA0S-09` (evidence hash `errstrings-upstream`), originally decided 2026-08-01.

full_description:
- Icon zoom is working, but the values seem to be off - see how Weakauras handles icon zoom

### Current implementation

`Icon:ApplyAppearance` in `modules/IconGrid_Render.lua` applies the setting as a symmetric `SetTexCoord` inset:

```lua
local z = cfg.zoom or 0.08
self.icon:SetTexCoord(z, 1 - z, z, 1 - z)
```

Schema row (`settings/Icons.lua`): `units.<unit>.icons.zoom`, `min = 0.0`, `max = 0.25`, `step = 0.01`, `default = 0.10`.

### Two concrete suspects for "the values seem off"

1. **Scale mismatch.** `z` is applied as the fraction cropped from *each* side, so `zoom = 0.10` removes 20% of the texture overall. If WeakAuras' slider means the *total* crop, the same number would crop twice as hard here — which reads exactly as "the values seem to be off" rather than "zoom is broken". **Unverified:** WeakAuras' actual convention needs checking against its source before acting on this.

2. **Two different defaults.** The DB/schema default is `0.10` (`core/Database.lua`, `settings/Icons.lua`) but the in-code fallback when `cfg.zoom` is nil is `0.08`. A profile that predates the setting renders at a different crop than a fresh one.

### Deciding what to do

Needs a call on which convention to adopt before any code changes:

- **Match WeakAuras** — treat the stored value as the total crop and apply `z/2` per side. Changes the appearance of every existing profile at the same stored number.
- **Keep per-side semantics, fix the labelling** — leave the maths alone and make the tooltip/range say what the number means, so it stops reading as a WeakAuras-compatible value.

Either way the `0.10` / `0.08` default mismatch should be reconciled to one number.

_(Detail added from a repo sweep; the original report is the first line above.)_

**Bug.** In `LibKa0s/Slash.lua` (v1.61.0), the file-level parsers `parseBool`, `allowedText` and `parseColor` read `lib.STRINGS` directly (around :281, :356, :381, :387), above `lib:New` (:484). A host's localized `L` overrides passed to its Slash instance therefore never reach them, and those strings always come out in the library's defaults.

**Consumer impact.** ConsumableMaster#16 ("Three Slash `L` overrides cannot be reached") is blocked on this: its `settings/Slash.lua:431-439` marks the three overrides dead. Any other host that localizes those strings has the same gap. Broader i18n is LibKa0s#6; this is the concrete defect.

**Fix direction.** Move the three parsers onto the instance (or pass the instance's string resolver into them) so they read the host's `L` like the rest of the Slash surface, bump Slash's LibStub minor, add a test that a host override is used, then re-vendor and close ConsumableMaster#16.

Found by the 2026-09-26 issue audit.

### Description
Currency-vendor refunds are now captured: when you refund a purchase paid for with a currency, the game returns the currency on `CHAT_MSG_CURRENCY` as a *"You are refunded: [currency]xN"* line. `Util.ParseSelfCurrency` now tags that line `REFUND`, and it records as a `Type=Currency` row with `source=Refund`, `CERTAIN` (branch `feature/currency-capture`).

Still **unhandled/unconfirmed**: refunds that return an **item** rather than a currency.

### Motivation
The loot-path REFUND handling — `Util.BuildLootPatterns` includes `LOOT_ITEM_REFUND` / `LOOT_ITEM_REFUND_MULTIPLE`, and `Collector:OnChatMsgLoot` attributes `directSource = REFUND` — is retained **speculatively** but has never been confirmed in-game. We have no in-client trace showing an item refund arriving on `CHAT_MSG_LOOT` as *"You are refunded: [item]"*. It may be dead code.

### Proposed behavior
Find an item-token vendor that refunds an **item** (not currency), capture the raw `CHAT_MSG_LOOT` line, and confirm the item records as `source=Refund`, `CERTAIN`. If item refunds never actually arrive on `CHAT_MSG_LOOT`, remove the dead loot-path REFUND handling instead.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] In-client trace captured of an item-returning refund (which event + exact string).
- [ ] If it arrives on `CHAT_MSG_LOOT`: `ParseSelfLoot` matches it, the item records as `source=Refund` / `CERTAIN`; add an end-to-end test + a smoke-test row.
- [ ] If it does **not** arrive on `CHAT_MSG_LOOT`: remove the speculative loot-path REFUND handling (patterns + collector branch) and its stale doc references.

- Interface: 120007 (WoW 12.0.7 Midnight)

title: Enemy damage taken belongs in its own window, not in a column
execution_status: referenced by 1 commit(s) on master; issue still open (partial or follow-up)
referencing_commits: e2e5075 2026-08-26 Take Enemy Damage Taken out of the grid, keep the read (#2)
summary: Status: decided, not started. Raised 2026-08-09. Migrated from the repo's TODO.md , which this issue store replaces. Updated 2026-08-26: the column has now been removed from the addon — see "What changed" below. EnemyDamageTaken was in the stat catalog ( core/Constants.lua ) with defaultEnabled = false , offered as one more column in the same grid as everything else. That is the wrong shape for it…
full_description:
**Status:** decided, not started. Raised 2026-08-09. Migrated from the repo's `TODO.md`, which this issue store replaces. **Updated 2026-08-26: the column has now been removed from the addon** — see "What changed" below.

`EnemyDamageTaken` was in the stat catalog (`core/Constants.lua`) with `defaultEnabled = false`, offered as one more column in the same grid as everything else. That is the wrong shape for it, and the reason is that it does not describe the same subject as its neighbors.

Every other column answers a question about **a group member**: how much damage did Alpha do, how many kicks did Beta land. `EnemyDamageTaken` answers a question about **an enemy**: how much damage did the boss take. Putting the two in one grid means one row has to be both a player and a mob, and the roster filter in `modules/Aggregator.lua` — which drops any source that is not a group member or an attributable pet — is written for the former and has to be special-cased for the latter.

What it should be instead: **a distinct window type** whose rows are enemies, with its own row identity (creature name and `sourceCreatureID` rather than player name, class and spec), its own default columns, and its own drill-down meaning — clicking an enemy row should break down *who* damaged it, which is a different pivot from the spell breakdown a player row gives.

### What changed — 2026-08-26

The column is **gone from the addon**, ahead of this work rather than as part of it. The original plan was to leave it in place until the window type landed ("a player who turns it on gets a column of numbers that are real, just oddly framed"); that was reversed because an oddly framed column in the shipped settings UI is a promise the grid cannot keep, and it is cheaper to remove it now than to explain it to every player who finds it.

**The catalog row was removed. The data was not.** `modules/Targets.lua` builds "which enemies this player hit" by walking that very meter column, and `core/Diagnostics.lua` probes it, so the read had to survive the column's removal. That split is now explicit in `core/Constants.lua`:

- `Constants.STAT_TYPE.EnemyDamageTaken` — **unchanged**. The enum value is still resolved.
- `Constants.STATS` — the `EnemyDamageTaken` row is **removed**. Everything that builds a column list walks this array: the Columns page's Add picker, the defaults, the aggregator's read loop, the sort-column dropdown, the CSV export, the tooltip's all-statistics list.
- `Constants.OFF_CATALOG_STATS` — **new**. A one-entry array holding the same descriptor, shaped like a catalog row because the provider takes it exactly as it takes one.
- `Constants.STAT_BY_KEY` — now means **"may this be a column"**, and answers nil for `EnemyDamageTaken`.
- `Constants.READABLE_STAT_BY_KEY` — **new**; the catalog plus the off-catalog reads. Means **"may this be read"**, and is the lookup `modules/Provider.lua` alone uses. Pointing the provider at the narrow lookup instead is what makes the Targets tooltip section go dark, and there is a test that fails if someone does.
- `Constants.STAT_COLORS.EnemyDamageTaken` — removed with the row. The palette is eight hues now.

**No migration, deliberately.** A profile that already holds an `EnemyDamageTaken` column keeps it in its saved variables. Every consumer resolves a stored column's `stat` string through `STAT_BY_KEY` and drops what it cannot resolve (`modules/Window.lua`, `modules/Aggregator.lua`, `modules/Export.lua`, `settings/Schema.lua`), and `settings/Columns.lua` deliberately still *lists* an unresolvable column so a player can see it and remove it by hand. That behavior predates this change and was written for exactly this case — a profile carried back from a build with more stats in its catalog.

**What this means for the work below.** The window type no longer has a column to migrate players off, which removes a step. It does mean the enemy read currently has exactly one consumer (`modules/Targets.lua`), so `OFF_CATALOG_STATS` exists to serve one caller; when the enemy window lands, the right question is whether that array is still the correct seam or whether the new window type should own its own stat catalog. Do not assume it stays.

### Notes for whoever picks this up

- `sourceCreatureID` is the join key for an enemy, not `sourceGUID`: an enemy GUID is per-spawn, so two pulls of the same mob are two GUIDs and one creature id. `Compat.GetCombatSessionSourceFromType` already takes a `sourceCreatureID` argument for exactly this, and `modules/Provider.lua` already forwards it.
- `Constants.SOURCE_DISPLAY_TYPE.Enemy` is how a source announces which side it is on, and the provider already copies `sourceDisplayType` onto every row it flattens. Nothing new has to be read.
- The roster filter's enemy gate in `modules/Aggregator.lua` **stays** and is still load-bearing. No column asks for an enemy source today, but the gate is what makes "no mob reaches the grid" a fact about that function rather than a fact about the column list.
- The window type would want its own entry in the window template rather than a flag on the existing one — `defaults/Profile.lua`'s `WINDOW_TEMPLATE` is one shape today, and a second shape is a schema change with a migration behind it (`core/Database.lua`).
- Tests that pin the current split: `Constants: EnemyDamageTaken is READABLE but is NOT a column` and `Constants: READABLE_STAT_BY_KEY is a superset of STAT_BY_KEY`, both in `tests/test_constants.lua`. The whole of `tests/test_targets.lua` is what proves the read still works.

title: S.Installed() has no caller — dead export, or an unwired guard
summary: Found by a dead-export sweep during the O.RefreshPanel adoption ( 630d1ea ), alongside P:RefreshPanels , which was removed in c596092 . This one was left in place because it is not the same kind of dead. What S.Installed() — modules/SunnArt.lua:246 — has zero callers anywhere in core/ , modules/ , settings/ , defaults/ or locales/ . lua function S.Installed() return S.Themes() 0 end Why it was not…
full_description:
Found by a dead-export sweep during the `O.RefreshPanel` adoption (`630d1ea`), alongside `P:RefreshPanels`, which was removed in `c596092`. This one was left in place because it is not the same kind of dead.

## What

`S.Installed()` — `modules/SunnArt.lua:246` — has **zero callers** anywhere in `core/`, `modules/`, `settings/`, `defaults/` or `locales/`.

```lua
function S.Installed()
  return #S.Themes() > 0
end
```

## Why it was not simply deleted

Three things make it heavier than an orphan:

1. **Its own comment claims a job nothing does.** It reads *"Used to keep the whole feature silent on a machine without it — no category, no rows, no settings copy about an addon the player does not have."* No code performs that gate through this function. The feature does stay silent, but by a different route: `modules/SunnArt.lua:466` calls `S.Themes()` directly and appends nothing when the list is empty. So the guard the comment describes is either redundant or was never wired.
2. **Six test assertions across four cases depend on it**, including one written specifically for it — *"SunnArt: Installed() agrees with the dropdown rather than with the globals"* (`tests/test_sunnart.lua:812`). Deleting the function means rewriting those as `#S.Themes() > 0`.
3. **It is documented as a deliberate design decision.** `docs/rendering.md:255` explains why it is defined as `#S.Themes() > 0` rather than as its own inspection of the Sunn globals: the earlier version returned true whenever any Sunn global existed, including for a SunnArt whose every theme named an uninstalled pack — so it could answer yes to a question the dropdown then answered no to. That reasoning is worth keeping whether or not the function is.

## The decision

Three ways to close this, and they are genuinely different:

- **Delete it.** Rewrite the six assertions as `#S.Themes() > 0`, and trim the last sentence of the `docs/rendering.md` paragraph (the folder-gate reasoning above it stays — it is about `S.Themes()` and is still live). Cheapest, and honest about what the code does.
- **Wire it.** If the comment describes a gate that *should* exist and does not, the fix is a caller, not a deletion. Worth checking whether the settings copy about Sunn is currently shown on a machine with no Sunn installed — if it is, this is a small bug rather than dead code.
- **Keep it as public surface.** If other addons are meant to be able to ask, say so in the comment and it stops looking accidental. Nothing currently documents it as public API and there is no `public-api` doc in this repo, so this is the weakest of the three.

## Not urgent

Zero runtime cost, zero user-visible effect, and the suite covers it either way. This is tidiness plus a comment that currently misdescribes the code.

## Where to look

- `modules/SunnArt.lua:238-248` — the function and its comment
- `modules/SunnArt.lua:466` — how the feature actually guards itself
- `tests/test_sunnart.lua:104, 115, 129, 687, 704, 812-821`
- `docs/rendering.md:248-257`

Wrap the frame system's member frames' `OnAttributeChanged` with `SecureHandlerWrapScript`, set up out of combat, so restricted code re-anchors (or re-points) the matching button in combat. Must be proven taint-free against EllesmereUI's SecureGroupHeader before shipping.

title: Complexity gate: lizard reads Lua's # length operator as a C preprocessor line and silently drops functions
summary: The automated-tests complexity gate runs lizard -l lua … -C 15 . Lizard's shared tokenizer treats as the start of a C preprocessor directive and throws away the rest of the line. In Lua, is the length operator. So when a keyword ( end , then , do , function , and , or , …) or an unbalanced brace follows on the same line, lizard never sees it, mis-nests the blocks, and drops whole functions from it…
full_description:
The automated-tests complexity gate runs `lizard -l lua … -C 15`. Lizard's shared tokenizer treats `#` as the start of a C preprocessor directive and throws away the rest of the line. In Lua, `#` is the length operator. So when a keyword (`end`, `then`, `do`, `function`, `and`, `or`, …) or an unbalanced brace follows `#` on the same line, lizard never sees it, mis-nests the blocks, and drops whole functions from its report.

Dropped functions are not measured at all. The gate stays silent and the bundle records a clean "max CCN" that isn't true.

## Minimal repro (lizard 1.24.0)

```lua
-- hidden.lua
local function a(t)
  for _, x in ipairs(t) do t[#t + 1] = x end
  return t
end

local function b(x)
  if x then return 1 end
  return 2
end
```

`lizard -l lua hidden.lua` lists only `b@6-9`; function `a` is gone. Put the loop body on its own line and both `a@1-6` and `b@8-11` are listed.

## Impact seen in AuraMaster

- 111 lines in 33 files hid **67 functions**: lizard listed 845 against 912 once `#` was stripped.
- Three hidden functions were over the limit: `FC.Compile` at CCN **42**, `Database.PrepareProfile` at about **21**, and `Helpers.RenderContainerPage` at **20**.
- The committed automated-test bundle still recorded "max CCN 15, 0 warnings".
- The usual idiom `t[#t + 1] = v end` on one line is enough to trigger it, so every Ka0s addon is likely affected.

Fixed on the AuraMaster branch `fix/review-audit-2026-09-11` (commit ba7d18a):
- Every hazardous line was rewritten equivalently: the length hoisted into a local, one-liners expanded, `find(prefix, 1, true) == 1`, and `t[1]` instead of `#t > 0`.
- The three functions were split below 15.
- A regression guard was added.

## Proposal

1. **Document it** in the complexity-gate section (automated-tests / testing): a `#` followed by a keyword or an unbalanced brace on the same line hides code from lizard, and the rule is to keep what follows a length operator on its own line or in a local.
2. **Ship a guard in the kit** (LibKa0s `testkit/`) so every consumer gets it. AuraMaster's local version is `tests/test_lintconfig.lua`, case "lintconfig: no length operator shares its line with a keyword or brace lizard must see". It strips comments and string contents from each line of every tracked non-vendored `.lua` file, then flags a line where a keyword lizard counts, or an unbalanced `{`/`}`, follows the first `#`. A balanced `{ … }` is allowed. The scanner self-tests on known-positive and known-negative lines.
3. **Optionally add a parity check to the runner:** compare the number of functions lizard lists per file with a `#`-stripped copy, and fail on any mismatch. That catches this and any future tokenizer blind spot.
4. **Re-run the complexity gate across the collection.** Existing "max CCN" figures from before the fix may be understated.

Found during the AuraMaster remediation (T29), after the review in `docs/reviews/2026-09-11` noted that lizard skipped `PrepareProfile`.

full_description:
### Description
The absorb bar's fill is currently scaled against the player's maximum health, which is not
configurable. A user reported that casting Ice Barrier for 174k absorb only fills the bar
roughly halfway, because their max health is much larger than the shield value.

### Motivation
Reported by @AdrianoCP on CurseForge:

> is it possible to define the max value of the bar that represents the full shield? For
> example, in my case, when I cast the ice barrier, the bar shows 174k of shield, but the bar
> is in the middle, like the total would be 350k or something like that. (...) it'd be good if
> the maximum is the real full shield health.

For classes whose shields are small relative to their health pool, the bar spends most of its
time in the lower portion of its range, which makes changes hard to read at a glance.

### Proposed behavior
Add a setting for how the bar maximum is derived, with the current behavior as the default:

- **Max health** (current default) — scale against `UnitHealthMax("player")`.
- **Shield peak** — scale against the largest absorb value seen for the current shield, so a
  freshly-cast shield starts full and drains to empty as it is consumed.
- **Custom value** — a user-entered fixed maximum.

### Acceptance criteria
- Existing users see no change in behavior unless they opt in.
- The bar mode is exposed in the settings panel and persists per profile.
- _TBD_ — exact reset semantics for "shield peak" (when a new shield replaces or stacks on an
  existing one) need to be pinned down during design.

title: Adopt O.RenderTabbedSchema opts for the Appearance page strip
summary: Evaluated under remediation item AT-15 (finding AbsorbTracker-A-04), against LibKa0s v1.56.0, Options 24.31.4.7.4 (OptionsTabs minor 4, which adds RenderTabbedSchema 's fifth opts argument: tabs , cfg , disabledFor , disabledNotice , chrome ). settings/UnitPanel.lua renderUnitPanelBody step 2 hand-builds the Appearance page's strip: partitionTabs , then Helpers.TabStrip , then RenderRows or render…
full_description:
Evaluated under remediation item AT-15 (finding AbsorbTracker-A-04), against LibKa0s v1.56.0, Options `24.31.4.7.4` (OptionsTabs minor 4, which adds `RenderTabbedSchema`'s fifth `opts` argument: `tabs`, `cfg`, `disabledFor`, `disabledNotice`, `chrome`).

`settings/UnitPanel.lua` `renderUnitPanelBody` step 2 hand-builds the Appearance page's strip: `partitionTabs`, then `Helpers.TabStrip`, then `RenderRows` or `renderMirroredHint`. The item adopts `O.RenderTabbedSchema(ctx, pageKey, nil, nil, { disabledFor = ..., disabledNotice = ... })` only if all four conditions hold.

| # | Condition | Holds at v1.56.0? |
|---|---|---|
| i | A `PageHeader` drawn before the call survives, and `ctx.__bannerHeight` still feeds the strip's reservation | Yes: `TabStrip` reads `ctx.__bannerHeight`, and `ClearScroll` leaves the chrome ledger alone |
| ii | Rows come from the descriptor's `rowsForPage(pageKey, ctx.unit)` | Yes: `OptionsTabs.lua` `O.RenderTabbedSchema` line 1457 |
| iii | `disabledFor(cfg)` is re-evaluated on every render and tab click | Yes: `pageDisabled(opts)` runs in `renderBody` on each render, and a tab click re-renders with the same `opts` |
| iv | `skipRender` rows stay out of the strip | **No.** `partition(rows)` (OptionsTabs.lua ~1332) keys on `row.group ~= nil` only, so the mirror flag row (`skipRender = true`, `group = "Link"`, settings/Appearance.lua) would become a sixth "Link" tab on target and focus |

**Failing condition: (iv).** Two more mismatches came up in the evaluation. Neither is one of the four conditions, but either would also block a like-for-like adoption:

- `disabledFor` draws `disabledNotice` **above** rows that are still drawn, disabled. This page draws the hint **in place of** the rows (the smoke test says "Focus with 'Linked to Player' shows the hint only"). The host cases in `tests/test_widgets.lua` pin this and would go red.
- The library's tab click is `ClearScroll` plus a re-render of `RenderTabbedSchema` alone. `ClearScroll` resets `ctx.refreshers`, so the page's two-tier mirror refresher would be gone after the first tab click.

The workaround would be a host tab keyed by each group whose `render` draws the hint, plus a `skipRender` filter on the host side. That means a local fork of the partition, which the spec lists as a non-goal. The host composition stays.

**Re-check trigger:** the next Options minor (OptionsTabs minor 5 or later). Adopt once `RenderTabbedSchema`'s partition skips `skipRender` rows. Then weigh the other two mismatches: a notice that replaces the rows rather than sitting above them, and a tab click that keeps host refreshers. The characterization cases added by AT-15 in `tests/test_widgets.lua` ("every unit's Appearance strip is its schema's groups…", "a mirrored unit's every tab draws the hint…") must stay green through an adoption.

It explicitly deferred the survey: "The candidate list above is triaged: each candidate accepted…
full_description:
### Description

Triage the candidate spell categories surveyed in #11, and ship the ones that earn it. This is
**Part B** of #11, split out so that issue could close on what actually shipped.

#11 delivered Part A (the Hard CC and Soft CC categories) and Part C (`tools/spell-research/`, the
repeatable derivation). It explicitly deferred the survey: *"The candidate list above is triaged:
each candidate accepted, deferred or dropped."* That criterion is this issue.

### Why this is cheap now

`tools/spell-research/research.py` already derives a category from the client's own DB2 data,
diffs it against the shipped lists and gates on a sentinel list. For any candidate backed by a
**spell mechanic**, adding a category is a new bucket in `BUCKET_MECHANICS`, a few sentinels, and an
accept pass over the diff — the same shape `hardCC` and `softCC` took.

### The constraint that shapes every debuff candidate

Blizzard honors spell ids only for **buffs on friendly units and debuffs on hostile ones**
(`FC.IdsAlwaysHonored` / `FC.IdsHonored`, `modules/FilterCompiler.lua`). So every debuff candidate
below works on a **hostile target or focus and nowhere else** — never on the player, never on party
members. "Am I silenced right now" is not answerable by a spell list, and that has to be said in the
UI the way the Hard CC and Soft CC rows already say it.

### Candidates — buffs (friendly units)

- [ ] **Immunities** — Divine Shield, Ice Block, Aspect of the Turtle, Cloak of Shadows, Blessing of
      Protection / Spellwarding, Netherwalk. Currently mixed into Defensive cooldowns, so this is a
      split of an existing list, not only an addition.
- [ ] **Bloodlust / Heroism** — Bloodlust, Heroism, Time Warp, Primal Rage, Fury of the Aspects, drums.
- [ ] **Racials** — Berserking, Blood Fury, Fireblood, Ancestral Call.
- [ ] **Raid buffs** — Arcane Intellect, Power Word: Fortitude, Battle Shout, Mark of the Wild,
      Skyfury, Blessing of the Bronze. Long-duration, for "missing buff" use.
- [ ] **Stealth / invisibility** — Stealth, Prowl, Shadowmeld, Invisibility, Camouflage.
- [ ] **Forms, stances and auras** — druid forms, warrior stances, paladin auras. Permanent clutter,
      mostly to Hide.
- [ ] **Resurrection effects** — Soulstone, Reincarnation readiness.
- [ ] **Procs** — Clearcasting, Hot Streak and similar. Large, class-specific, and the highest
      maintenance of the set.
- [ ] **Seasonal / content buffs** — Mythic+ affix buffs, delve boons, the current tier's helpful
      mechanics. Changes every season, so this one depends most on the research process.
- [ ] **Cosmetic / toys / world buffs** — mostly for hiding clutter.

### Candidates — debuffs (hostile units)

- [ ] **Silences** — Silence, Solar Beam, Strangulate, Sigil of Silence, Spell Lock, Garrote.
      Mechanic 9 `silenced`, derivable today.
- [ ] **Disarms** — Disarm, Grapple Weapon, Dismantle. Mechanic 3 `disarmed`, derivable today.
- [ ] **Taunts** — Taunt, Growl, Hand of Reckoning, Provoke, Dark Command, Torment. Mechanic 36
      `taunted`, derivable today. For tanks.
- [ ] **Healing reduction** — Mortal Strike / Mortal Wounds, Wound Poison. PvP.
- [ ] **Raid debuffs on enemies** — Mystic Touch, Chaos Brand, Hunter's Mark.
- [ ] **Your DoTs** — a per-class damage-over-time list, to show only your rotation's debuffs.

### Candidates — not spell lists (new kinds), each needs the engine verified first

- [ ] A **nameplate-relevant** flag category (`nameplateShowAll` / `nameplateShowPersonal`).
- [ ] **Enrage** as a dispel-type category for hostile buffs (Soothe / Tranquilizing Shot targets).

- [ ] Each candidate above is marked accepted, deferred or dropped, with the reason recorded.

title: Offer real choices for the pandemic highlight: what it covers, and what it looks like
summary: Description The refresh-window ("pandemic") highlight is one fixed effect: a flat additive wash over the whole element, in one color. Offer real choices — what it covers, and what it looks like. What ships today - Bars and Icons : a single WHITE_TEXTURE texture, SetAllPoints(frame) , SetBlendMode("ADD") , tinted by pandemicColor , handed to the engine with AddPandemicRegion ( modules/Style_Bars.lu…
full_description:
### Description

The refresh-window ("pandemic") **highlight** is one fixed effect: a flat additive wash over the
whole element, in one color. Offer real choices — what it covers, and what it looks like.

### What ships today

- **Bars and Icons**: a single `WHITE_TEXTURE` texture, `SetAllPoints(frame)`, `SetBlendMode("ADD")`,
  tinted by `pandemicColor`, handed to the engine with `AddPandemicRegion`
  (`modules/Style_Bars.lua:73-79,289,329`; `modules/Style_Icons.lua:52-56,170`). One look, one color,
  whole element, on or off.
- **Text**: **no highlight at all.** The Text page's Pandemic tab only recolors the duration tokens
  (`settings/Text.lua:449-453`); `modules/Style_Text.lua` never binds `AddPandemicRegion` — a grep
  for `pandemic` in that file returns nothing. So a text container's "Pandemic" settings do
  something genuinely different from the other two styles', which is not obvious from the UI.

#### Text already owns the regions it needs (owner, 2026-09-21)

Text does not need a new region invented for it: **put the glow on the same border the dispel colors
already use.** Those regions exist and are already handed to the engine:

- `am.backdrop`, a `BACKGROUND` texture (`modules/Style_Text.lua:113`);
- four edge strips — `edgeTop`, `edgeBottom`, `edgeLeft`, `edgeRight` — built as `BORDER` textures
  from the `EDGES` table (`modules/Style_Text.lua:72-77`, `:116-119`).

`dispelTints` hands whichever of them the player turned on to the engine with
`AddDispelTypeTexture` (`modules/Style_Text.lua:490-496`). Binding those same regions with
`AddPandemicRegion` is the identical shape of call, on regions that already exist, in a file that
already clears its additive list at the head of the dress
(`Style.ClearAdditiveBindings`, `modules/Style_Text.lua:551`).

That makes Text the **cheapest** of the three styles to fix rather than the hardest, and it makes
*border glow* the option to build first — it is the one that needs no new region on any style, since
bars and icons own borders too.

The open question it raises, which belongs in the design: a region bound to **both**
`AddDispelTypeTexture` and `AddPandemicRegion` is on two additive lists at once. What the engine
does when both want to tint the same texture is exactly the thing to test before building on it, and
`docs/midnight-quirks.md:196` is the reason to expect a surprise there.

### The constraint that shapes every option here

**Aura data is secret in combat**, so the addon cannot watch a timer and light a glow itself
(`docs/scope.md` → *Out of reach*, `core/Secrets.lua`). Today's highlight works only because the
addon builds the region up front and hands it to the engine through `AddPandemicRegion`; **the engine
decides when to show it**, in its own secure code.

That is the hinge for this whole issue. Any option below is achievable only if it can be expressed
as **a region (or set of regions) the engine shows and hides**, not as an effect driven by addon Lua
during combat. A per-frame animated glow whose frames we drive is out of reach for the same reason
a minimum-duration filter is. Options are marked accordingly, and *(verify)* means the engine
support has not been confirmed.

Second constraint, already bitten once: `AddDispelTypeTexture` and `AddPandemicRegion` **append** to
the button, and a restyle that clears them can leave a stale list (`docs/midnight-quirks.md:196`,
and the Icons border case at `:315-328`). More regions per button makes that sharper, not softer.

### What to offer — scope of the highlight

Which part of the element the highlight covers, per style:

- **Whole element** — today's behavior, and the default.
- **The icon only** — on a bar, wash the icon and leave the bar alone (and the reverse).
- **The bar fill only** — so the highlight rides the fill's moving edge rather than the frame.
- **The border / edge only** — recolor or thicken the existing border instead of washing the middle.
  Cheap, since bars, icons and text already own border regions.
- **The text only** — recolor name/time/stacks. **Text already does exactly this** and calls it
  Pandemic; unifying the vocabulary is half the work of this issue.

### What to offer — the look

- **Solid wash** *(ships today)* — flat additive tint.
- **Border glow** — tint or thicken the existing edge. **The one to build first.** Most likely to
  be reachable, because the regions already exist on all three styles and it is still just a texture
  the engine toggles — see the Text note above, where the dispel border is exactly this.
- **Pixel glow** — the marching-pixel border effect players know from LibCustomGlow. Would mean
  either vendoring that library or building an equivalent. *(verify — its animation is normally
  driven by an `OnUpdate`, which is the thing the secrecy rule forbids; the question is whether a
  looping `AnimationGroup` on a handed-over region survives, since the engine drives visibility
  rather than the animation.)*
- **Action-button proc glow** — Blizzard's own spell-alert overlay
  (`ActionButton_ShowOverlayGlow` / the spell-alert manager). Instantly familiar. *(verify — these
  are built for action buttons and attach to a button's own frame; whether one can be attached to an
  aura button we do not own, and driven by the engine's show/hide, is exactly what to test first.)*
- **Assisted-highlight style** — the newer assisted-combat rotation highlight. *(verify, same
  question, plus whether the API is public at all on 12.1.)*
- **Autocast shine** — the spinning-sparkle overlay. *(verify)*
- **Pulse / blink** — the addon already ships `pulse`, `blink` and `bounce` for text
  (`core/Constants.lua:195`). If an `AnimationGroup` can loop on an engine-shown region, this is the
  cheapest "animated" option and reuses vocabulary the panel already has. *(verify)*
- **Desaturate or dim the element instead of brightening it** — the inverse highlight, which reads
  better on a bright icon than any glow does.

### Other things that make sense

- **More than one window.** Today there is one threshold. A second (say 30% and 10%) with its own
  look would let "refreshable" and "about to drop" read differently.
- **Per-container, not just per-style.** Confirm how this interacts with the per-container model
  before designing the schema.
- **Interaction with the existing Time color.** Both fire in the same window; a player turning both
  on gets two effects at once and nothing says so.
- **Interaction with dispel coloring**, which already binds additive regions to the same button.
- **A none/off option that is explicit**, rather than "highlight on with a transparent color".
- **Test-mode coverage** — `modules/Preview.lua` must show the chosen highlight, or the player
  cannot see what they picked without waiting for a real aura.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Highlight scope is selectable per style, with today's whole-element behavior as the default.
- [ ] At least one alternative look ships beyond the solid wash, chosen from the options above that
      survive the engine check.
- [ ] Every option marked *(verify)* is settled — implemented or recorded as out of reach with the
      rule that makes it so, the way `docs/scope.md` records the others.
- [ ] Text's Pandemic tab either gains a real highlight — on the dispel border, per the note above — or is relabeled so it stops implying one.
- [ ] Settled: what the engine does with a region on BOTH the dispel and the pandemic additive list.
- [ ] The additive-binding staleness (`docs/midnight-quirks.md:196`) is re-checked against however
      many regions the new options add.
- [ ] Test mode draws the highlight.
- [ ] `docs/settings-panel.md`, `docs/scope.md` and the smoke-test checklist updated.

### Related

- #7 — sorting/group behavior; more regions per button interacts with group count.

full_description:
## Summary

Let containers snap to each other by drag and drop in unlock mode, and let a drag break the snap again.

## Requested behaviour

- **Drag to attach.** While unlocked, dragging a container's anchor close to another container snaps it onto that container. This sets the Layout > Anchor "Attach to" mode to *Another container*, with the dragged container as the child.
- **Drag to detach.** Dragging an attached container far enough away breaks the attachment and returns it to screen-anchor mode, at the position where it was dropped.
- **Richer anchor points (optional, still needs design).** Widen the *Another container* options so the parent and child anchor points can be chosen (for example, child TOPLEFT to parent BOTTOMLEFT, or child LEFT to parent RIGHT). Today the attachment point is fixed and depends on the container type.

## Open design questions

- Snap threshold and visual feedback: highlight the target container while hovering in range?
- Choosing the anchor point from the drop position: nearest edge, or nearest of the 8 points?
- Cycles: A cannot attach to B if B is already attached to A, directly or through a chain.
- How detaching interacts with the X/Y offset sliders.
- Should holding a modifier key (e.g. Shift) suppress snapping?

Raised in the 2026-09-25 feedback batch (item 5). Deferred on purpose; think it through at implementation time.

full_description:
Deferred from the initial macro bar feature (`docs/macro-bar.md`). The bar ships with no keybinding support — users who want a key on a Consumable Master macro bind it on a normal Blizzard action bar instead.

**What this would add**

A keybind per bar slot, set from the Macro Bar settings page, so the bar is usable without ever touching a Blizzard bar.

**Sketch**

- A `SecureHandlerBaseTemplate` parent for the bar plus `SetOverrideBindingClick(handler, true, key, buttonName)` per bound slot.
- Bindings applied out of combat only, re-applied on login and after any reorder; queued to `PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED` like every other protected operation the bar performs (see the combat contract in `docs/macro-bar.md`).
- Persist as `db.profile.macroBar.binds[catKey] = "<key>"`. Not a schema scalar — it's a dynamic per-category map, like `shown`.
- Panel UI: a keybinding capture widget per row in the *Macros on the bar* section. AceGUI ships a `Keybinding` widget (`libs/AceGUI-3.0/widgets/AceGUIWidget-Keybinding.lua`) that is already vendored and currently unused.
- Optional: render the bound key as text in the corner of each button, and a setting to show/hide it.

**Open questions**

- Whether to use override bindings (invisible to Blizzard's Key Bindings UI, simple, addon-owned) or real named bindings via a `Bindings.xml` (visible in the Key Bindings UI, but a fixed set of 13 headers and clumsier).
- Conflict handling when the chosen key is already bound elsewhere.

full_description:
Deferred from the initial macro bar feature (`docs/macro-bar.md`). When a category has nothing to pick — no food in bags, no flask for the current spec — its macro is in the empty state and the bar slot simply shows the macro's own fallback icon (the cooking pot) at full opacity. Functionally fine (clicking it prints the category's "no X in bags" message), but visually indistinguishable from a slot that's ready to use.

**What this would add**

A setting for how an empty slot presents itself:

- **Normal** (today's behaviour) — the macro's fallback icon, undimmed.
- **Dim / desaturate** — icon desaturated at a configurable alpha, so ready-to-use slots stand out.
- **Hide, keep the gap** — slot invisible, grid position reserved, so the bar's shape never changes.
- **Hide and reflow** — slot removed and later slots shift up. Note: this makes the bar's size change during play, and the relayout is a protected-frame operation, so it would have to be deferred out of combat — worth deciding whether it's worth supporting at all.

Also consider a matching "hide the whole bar when every slot is empty" toggle.

**Where it goes**

`modules/MacroBarButton.lua` (`ApplyStyle` / `RefreshIcon` — `KCM.MacroDisplay.PickID(macroName) == nil` is the empty test) plus a schema row in `settings/MacroBar.lua`. The hide-and-reflow variant additionally needs `MacroBarModel.Visible()` to filter on the live pick state and a relayout hook on `MACROBAR_REFRESH`.

full_description:
A settings panel opened in a fresh session while ConsumableMaster is disabled shows `[Loading]` for any item row whose name is not already cached. It stays that way until the addon is re-enabled.

**Why.** The stand-down drops both hydration triggers: `UnregisterAllEvents` removes `GET_ITEM_INFO_RECEIVED` (`core/LifecycleSetup.lua`), and the options bus target's `PANEL_REFRESH` subscription is taken down (`settings/OptionsShim.lua`). The row falls back to `[Loading]` in `modules/KCMItemRow.lua:84-99` (`itemDisplayName`).

**Possible fix.** Let the panel hydrate its own rows while disabled through LibKa0s-Item's `LoadItem`, which `core/ItemSetup.lua:14-16` declines today on the grounds that the pipeline's `GET_ITEM_INFO_RECEIVED` path already hydrates. That path doesn't run while the addon is disabled.

**Needs an owner decision.** slash-commands-§7 records the panel-refresh-while-disabled question as "Recorded, not ruled". The impact is cosmetic: only uncached, non-bag item names in a panel opened while disabled.

Source: 2026-09-23 review finding ConsumableMaster-R-04 (review F-004), remediation item CM-14.

full_description:
### Description

`Icon:Apply` currently does all cooldown rendering — the alpha/tint/GCD-suppression curve evaluations, the swipe re-arm, and the countdown text — and it only runs when `Cooldowns` emits `Ka0s_KickCD_SPELL_STATE`. Because that emit is forced to fire ~10x/sec for any spell on cooldown (see Background), the emit is effectively acting as the animation driver for those visuals.

This proposes inverting that: let the existing 0.1s ticker in `modules/IconGrid_Render.lua` own everything time-varying, so `Cooldowns` can emit only on genuine state transitions.

### Background — why the emit rate is currently fixed

`C_Spell.GetSpellCooldownDuration` mints a **fresh object on every call**, so `Cooldowns.StateChanged`'s `prev.cdObject ~= next_.cdObject` compare is true on every poll for any spell on cooldown.

That compare cannot simply be replaced. Measured on a live 12.0.7 client via `/kcd debug duration` (results recorded in `docs/midnight-quirks.md`): **in combat every `DurationObject` getter is secret-tainted, including the booleans** — `HasExpired`, `HasStarted`, `IsActive`, `IsZero`. A secret boolean can't be branched on. Only `HasSecretValues()` stays plain.

So there is no Lua-side way to detect "this spell's cooldown changed" in combat. The identity compare over-fires but never under-fires, and nothing on the object can replace it.

**The ticker approach sidesteps this entirely** — re-fetching the handle each tick is unconditionally correct, so there is nothing to detect.

### Motivation

Already addressed in 9fc0d8b by splitting `Icon:Apply` into state-work vs time-work and gating the state half — a **measured 35%** reduction in widget calls per repeat apply. This issue is the remaining, larger half.

Baseline in combat (4 spells on cooldown, target+focus enabled, ~10 events/sec):

| | Now | After |
|---|---|---|
| `Icon:Apply` calls/sec | 80 | ~0 |
| C calls/sec | ~1600 | ~880 |
| Table allocations/sec | 80 | 40 |

The stronger argument is structural rather than performance. ~1600 C calls/sec is not a framerate problem. But today there's no rule about what may be added to `Icon:Apply`, which is why `Icon:StartGlow` needed a bespoke idempotency gate to stop a visible ButtonGlow pop at 10Hz. Removing the 10Hz emit makes that trap stop existing rather than needing to be remembered.

### Proposed behavior

- **Ticker (0.1s)** — for each icon with an active cooldown: fetch a fresh handle, evaluate the three curves, apply alpha/tint/suppression, re-arm the swipe, update the countdown text. Stop when `C_Spell.GetSpellCooldown(...).isActive` goes false — that stays **plain** in combat and is what `Cooldowns:PollSpell` already relies on.
- **Emit** — only on material change (`ready` / `isActive` / handle presence / plain charges) -> glow, charges badge, branch selection, ticker register/unregister.
- **`StateChanged`** — drop the `cdObject` / `chargeCdObject` identity compares. `MaterialChange` (added in the parent commit as a log gate) then folds back into it.

Rule to preserve: **emit = state changed, ticker = time passed.**

### Known constraints

- Ticker registration is currently gated on `cfg.showCooldownText`; it must become "any icon with an active cooldown" or curve updates stop when the user disables cooldown text.
- Branch 2 (charge recharge, `chargeCdObject`) needs the same treatment as branch 1.
- `GetSpellCooldownDuration` returns a **zeroed object, not nil**, for an idle spell — a non-nil handle is not an "is on cooldown" signal.
- `Assign()`/`Copy()` exist and work, but offer little here: you still fetch a fresh object to assign *from*, so the allocation remains.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `SPELL_STATE` emits for a spell on an unchanged cooldown drop to ~0 (verify with `/kcd debug on`)
- [ ] Curve-driven visuals still update — in particular the icon brightening from cooldown alpha/tint to ready visuals in a cooldown's final ~1.6s (the `GCD_UPPER` step)
- [ ] Swipe animates smoothly with no stutter or restart
- [ ] Countdown text ticks continuously; charges badge stays live in combat where the count is secret
- [ ] Config changes (glow type/colour, cooldown text toggle) still take effect mid-cooldown
- [ ] No errors in combat — the whole point is that everything stays C-side
- [ ] `docs/smoke-tests.md` §9c passes
- [ ] `lua tests/run.lua` and `luacheck .` clean

### Environment

KickCD 1.2.0, Interface 120007. Related: 9fc0d8b (the 35% half + probe), `/kcd debug duration`, `docs/midnight-quirks.md`.

title: Adopt RenderGrid for the spell-list editor — blocked on two LibKa0s gaps
summary: Description LibKa0s-Options-1.0 shipped RenderGrid in OptionsWidgets minor 4 as the caller-driven sibling of RenderRows — for lists whose length is not in the schema . Its stated rationale was that "every host had a hand-rolled copy of this loop". KickCD has exactly one such list — the spell-list editor — and RenderGrid currently cannot reach it . A read-only recon during the 2026-08-01 adoption r…
full_description:
### Description

`LibKa0s-Options-1.0` shipped `RenderGrid` in `OptionsWidgets` minor 4 as the caller-driven sibling of `RenderRows` — for lists whose **length is not in the schema**. Its stated rationale was that "every host had a hand-rolled copy of this loop".

KickCD has exactly one such list — the spell-list editor — and `RenderGrid` currently **cannot reach it**. A read-only recon during the 2026-08-01 adoption report returned `not-expressible`, and the reason is two gaps in the library rather than anything bespoke about this addon.

The list in question is `settings/Spells.lua:913`:

```lua
for i = 1, #list do container:AddChild(buildRow(AceGUI, list, i)) end
```

One row per tracked spell for the selected class/spec, length coming from the profile's spell table. `buildRow` (`settings/Spells.lua:506`) builds a 28px full-width `SimpleGroup(Flow)` of eight fixed-pixel-width widgets. Rows are reorderable and removable at runtime.

### Motivation

`RenderGrid` currently has exactly **one** consumer (ConsumableMaster). A surface with one consumer has had its contract tested against one shape, and every adopter so far has surfaced a descriptor assumption that only held for the ones before it. Making KickCD's spell list a real second consumer is worth more than the lines it would retire.

It also corrects a standing claim: `LibKa0s/docs/adoption-prompt.md` records ~450 lines across `settings/Panel.lua`, `Panel_Widgets.lua` and `Panel_Render.lua` as having "no library equivalent". That assessment **predates `RenderGrid`**, and it still stands — but for a reason it never recorded, which is finding 1 below.

### Proposed behavior

Both fixes are upstream in `../LibKa0s`, additive within `-1.0`, and neither can be worked around here. **Never edit `libs/` — the next re-vendor reverts it silently.**

**1. `RenderGrid` needs a `parent` parameter (blocking).**

`libs/LibKa0s/OptionsWidgets.lua:534-535`:

```lua
function O.RenderGrid(ctx, items)
  local scroll = O.EnsureScroll(ctx)   -- hard-bound
```

`EnsureScroll` caches on `ctx.scroll` and anchors its ScrollFrame flush to the whole of `ctx.body` (`libs/LibKa0s/Options.lua:289-290`, `TOPLEFT PADDING_X-4,-8` / `BOTTOMRIGHT -(PADDING_X+12),8`).

`settings/Spells.lua:888` creates **its own** ScrollFrame, anchored `TOPLEFT body 16,-56` to leave room for a hand-anchored header, and applies `PatchAlwaysShowScrollbar` to that container itself. Calling `RenderGrid` there would silently instantiate a second, full-body scroll frame overlapping the header.

`RenderGrid` is the only maker in the module that does not take a parent. Seven siblings already do it the right way — `RenderField(ctx, row, parent, relativeWidth)` at `:464`, `SessionCheckbox` at `:481`, and five makers using `parent = parent or O.EnsureScroll(ctx)` (`:255`, `:276`, `:333`, `:375`, `:395`, `:482`).

Proposed: `RenderGrid(ctx, items, parent)` with the same `parent or O.EnsureScroll(ctx)` default. Additive, preserves today's behavior for the existing consumer, and is the single change that makes this adoptable.

**2. `RenderGrid` never calls `DoLayout()`.**

`RenderRows` ends with `if scroll.DoLayout then scroll:DoLayout() end` (`OptionsWidgets.lua:657`). `RenderGrid` ends at `flushRow()` and returns. A host that renders a page with `RenderGrid` **alone** — the whole point of a caller-driven sibling — gets an unlaid-out scroll frame and has to know to call `DoLayout` itself. The README entry does not say so. Either match `RenderRows` or document the asymmetry.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `RenderGrid` accepts an optional `parent`, defaulting to `O.EnsureScroll(ctx)`; ConsumableMaster's existing call is unchanged in behavior.
- [ ] The `DoLayout` asymmetry is resolved — matched to `RenderRows` or documented in `LibKa0s/README.md`.
- [ ] Both land upstream in `../LibKa0s` with a failing test first, the touched files' minors bumped, `CHANGELOG.md` updated, and a re-vendor into **every** consumer (`LibKa0s/docs/releasing.md`). Each existing consumer's suite must be unchanged — that is what proves the change was additive.
- [ ] `settings/Spells.lua:913` renders through `RenderGrid`, with the row strip visually unchanged.
- [ ] Smoke test §25 and §10 (spell-list editor) pass.

### Out of scope / notes

Two further `RenderGrid` limits were found and are **not** blockers for this issue — the spell row would still be one opaque `wide` item whose `make` builds the strip, so adoption retires little of `buildRow`:

- Only two cell widths exist: `HALF` (0.5) or full-width via `wide`. A dense multi-column list needs a per-item `width`, or an items-per-row parameter.
- `O.AddSpacer(scroll, L.ROW_VSPACER)` fires unconditionally after every flushed row (`:548`, `:575`) with no opt-out. The spell list is a compact 28px List layout with no inter-row gap, so it would change visually.

Separately, the `wide` branch adds its SimpleGroup **and** its spacer even when the item's render returned false, leaving a blank gap where a failing item was. The paired branch is correct. Guard-per-item is the stated contract; the wide path only half-honours it.

Source: `LibKa0s/docs/adoption/2026-08-01/` (§7 of `03_DEVIATIONS.md` / `04_RECOMMENDATIONS.md`), and the recon recorded in `docs/pending/LEDGER.md`.

summary: Bug. When the Text Label is attached to the cast bar , toggling the label (Show label on/off, or changing what it attaches to) does not move the cast bar's own drag handle until a /reload . Why. modules/Castbar_Handle.lua places the cast bar handle once, at build. The 2026-09-26 fix for the icon grid's handle (KickCD master cdff980's predecessor 604e922: "the unlocked drag handle sits above the un…
full_description:
**Bug.** When the Text Label is attached to the **cast bar**, toggling the label (Show label on/off, or changing what it attaches to) does not move the cast bar's own drag handle until a `/reload`.

**Why.** `modules/Castbar_Handle.lua` places the cast bar handle once, at build. The 2026-09-26 fix for the icon grid's handle (KickCD master cdff980's predecessor 604e922: "the unlocked drag handle sits above the unit label, not over it") made `IconGrid:OnConfigChanged` re-run `ApplyLock` on a `label` change, but the cast bar handle has no equivalent path. At load, a label on the cast bar is cleared correctly; only the toggle is missed.

**Who hits it.** Only a setup with the label attached to the cast bar and the cast bar in a mode that shows its own handle. The owner's setup (label on icons, cast bar anchor mode PRIMARY, which hides that handle) does not.

**Fix direction.** Mirror the icon grid: re-place the cast bar handle on `CONFIG_CHANGED { section = "label" }`, with a headless test that toggles the label over the bus (no manual ApplyLock) and asserts the handle's anchor.

Found by the independent review of the unlocked-handle fix (2026-09-26).

The label text is centred on a 1x1 frame placed 12px above the grid ( defaults/Profile.lua:270-274 : point BOTTOM, relPoint TOP, offsetY 12). The frame does not grow with the font, so a tall font extends below that point, over the icons. This is separate from the drag-handle overlap fixed on 2026…
full_description:
**Bug.** With a very large Text Label font, the label's lower half can reach down into the icon grid.

**Why.** The label text is centred on a 1x1 frame placed 12px above the grid (`defaults/Profile.lua:270-274`: point BOTTOM, relPoint TOP, offsetY 12). The frame does not grow with the font, so a tall font extends below that point, over the icons. This is separate from the drag-handle overlap fixed on 2026-09-26 (604e922), which now hangs off the label text itself and clears any font size; this one is label versus icons, and it predates that fix.

**Fix direction.** Anchor the label by its bottom edge (size the label frame to the text, or anchor the FontString's BOTTOM to the grid's TOP plus the offset) so it always grows upward, with a test that sets a large font and asserts the label's bottom stays at or above the grid's top.

Found by the independent review of the unlocked-handle fix (2026-09-26).

title: Perf: in-combat and out-of-combat capture variants
summary: Description LibKa0s-Perf-1.0 currently only measures one way: a measurement window is armed ( measure a / measure b ), and recording starts the moment combat starts and ends when combat ends. Everything outside combat is deliberately not measured. Add an out-of-combat variant alongside the existing in-combat one, so a host can run an experiment in whichever mode actually reflects how it is used. M…
full_description:
### Description

`LibKa0s-Perf-1.0` currently only measures one way: a measurement window is armed
(`measure a` / `measure b`), and recording starts the moment combat starts and ends
when combat ends. Everything outside combat is deliberately not measured.

Add an **out-of-combat variant** alongside the existing in-combat one, so a host can
run an experiment in whichever mode actually reflects how it is used.

### Motivation

Not every adopter does meaningful work in combat. BankLedger and LootHistory are
out-of-combat addons — the current combat-gated protocol has nothing to measure for
them, which is part of why neither has a Perf module built today. An out-of-combat
variant is what makes Perf adoptable across the whole collection rather than only the
combat-facing addons (AbsorbTracker, KickCD, ConsumableMaster).

### Proposed behavior

- Two capture variants — in-combat (today's behavior, unchanged) and out-of-combat.
- Hosts declare which variant(s) apply to them; an addon may support only one.
- Work out how the **measure step** is bounded out of combat. The in-combat window has
  natural start and end edges (`PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED` / `_ENABLED`); out of combat there
  is no such edge, so the window needs some other terminator — a fixed-duration timer, an
  explicit stop verb, or something else. This is the open design question. _TBD_
- The `/xx perf` step panel changes: the step list and its wording are written around
  "arm, wait for combat, combat ends" and will need to represent the out-of-combat flow.
- Roll the change out to all adopters after the library change lands.

### Acceptance criteria

- `LibKa0s-Perf-1.0` supports both an in-combat and an out-of-combat capture variant.
- The out-of-combat measure step has a defined, documented way of bounding the window.
- The `/xx perf` panel and `perf` command help render correctly for both variants, and
  for a host that supports only one.
- All adopters are updated: AbsorbTracker, KickCD and ConsumableMaster keep working on
  the existing in-combat path; BankLedger and LootHistory gain out-of-combat Perf modules.
- `docs/releasing.md`'s Consumers table is updated for the new `LibKa0s-Perf-1.0` adopters.

full_description:
### Description

LibKa0s has no localization layer. Every user-facing string across the library
(and the addons that consume it) is a hardcoded English literal. This issue
covers building a localization framework in LibKa0s, routing all existing
English strings through it, and then rolling the resulting pattern out to the
Ka0s WoW Addon Standard and every Ka0s addon.

### Motivation

- Ka0s addons are English-only today, which shuts out non-English WoW clients.
- Hardcoded English strings are also a correctness hazard: any code that
  *matches against* an English string rather than an ID or enum will silently
  break the moment the string is translated (or the client locale changes).

  free rather than each reinventing it.

### Proposed behavior

  enums. Flag every occurrence and fix it — string comparison must never be
  load-bearing.

- Provide a localization API in LibKa0s covering all existing user-facing
  strings, and designed so newly added strings drop into it naturally.
- Fallback: when a localized string is missing for the active locale, fall back
  to the English string. Never render a raw key or `nil`.
- Support the full set of Blizzard-supported client locales as the initial
  target set.

**Adoption**
- Convert every English string in LibKa0s itself to go through the framework.
- Add the finalized pattern to the Ka0s WoW Addon Standard
  (`WowAddonStandards`) as a standards section.
- Adopt across all Ka0s addons.

**Documentation**
- New `LOCALIZATION.md` documenting the contributor workflow — what someone who
  wants to help translate needs to do, step by step. Linked from `README.md`.
- Document the supported locale list and the % translation coverage per locale,
  kept current as translations land.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Analysis of all Ka0s addons is complete and a localization pattern is chosen, with rationale recorded.
- [ ] All English-string matching is identified and replaced with ID/enum comparison.
- [ ] All user-facing strings in LibKa0s go through the localization framework.
- [ ] A missing localized string falls back to English, verified by test.
- [ ] All Blizzard-supported locales are registered as targets.
- [ ] `LOCALIZATION.md` exists, documents the contributor workflow, and is linked from `README.md`.
- [ ] Supported locales and per-locale % coverage are documented.
- [ ] The pattern is added to the WowAddonStandards repo.
- [ ] All Ka0s addons have adopted the framework.
