full_description:
### Description

`LibKa0s/Perf.lua` is **1163 LOC**, inside `layout-§1`'s 1000–1500 *on notice* band. It is the
only shipped file in the band and the widest surface consumers bind against.

This issue exists to **discharge a shelf-life obligation, not to schedule a split.** The file is
under the 1500 cap, so nothing is in violation. `automated-tests-§4` (anti-pattern #53) says a
watch-list disposition carried as *Accepted* across three consecutive **release** runs is owed
either a fix or a tracked deviation ID with an owner. This one has been carried through v1.8.0
(`20260805-123655`), v1.8.1 (`20260806-180959`) and v1.8.2 (`20260807-105553`), so the clock
expired at v1.8.2. This is the ID.

### Why it is not being split now

The diagnosis is **breadth, not knots** — worst function in the file is `groupContext` at CCN 11,
and the file's average CCN is 3.4. There is no tangle to unpick.

Splitting a *library* file also costs more than splitting an addon file: it touches `LibKa0s.xml`
load order, the LibStub major boundaries, and every consumer that vendors `libs/LibKa0s/` **whole**
(anti-pattern #48). Spending that churn to move a file from 1163 to two files around 580 each, with
337 lines of headroom under the cap, buys nothing a reader or a consumer can feel.

### The plan if it does cross 1500

The peel seam is already identified: **the sampler** and **the group/scenario bookkeeping** are the
two coherent halves. `layout-§1` MAYs a peel into 2–3 sibling files in the same folder, so the
shape would be `LibKa0s/Perf.lua` + `LibKa0s/Perf_Sampler.lua` (or similar), both listed in
`LibKa0s.xml` in dependency order, with the LibStub major unchanged so no consumer re-binds.

### Trigger

- **Hard:** the file crosses **1500 LOC** — at that point `layout-§1` is a MUST failure and the peel
  above is executed, not re-argued.
- **Soft:** re-read at each release run. The figure has been static at 1163 since
  `20260805-002859`; it last grew for the observed-containment record and the keyed `Open`/`Close`
  bracket.

### Disposition recorded in the record

`docs/automated-tests/RESULTS.md` → `## Complexity watch list` → *Files by `layout-§1` band* now
reads **Already tracked as this issue** rather than *Accepted, expired*.

title: Establish today's zero-consumer export set, and retire the host duplicates behind it
summary: LibKa0s carries public exports that no host calls, while the addons still ship their own duplicates of the same behaviour. Under -1.0 's frozen additive-only rule there is no deprecation available, so every one of those exports is permanent — which makes "who actually calls this" a question worth answering once, deliberately, rather than re-deriving per adoption cycle. full_description:
LibKa0s carries public exports that no host calls, while the addons still ship their own duplicates of
the same behaviour. Under `-1.0`'s frozen additive-only rule there is no deprecation available, so
every one of those exports is permanent — which makes "who actually calls this" a question worth
answering once, deliberately, rather than re-deriving per adoption cycle.

Filed as discovery. The first task is measurement, because the three records the repo already has
**disagree with each other**, and none of them is today's number.

## What the existing records say

**1. `docs/adoption-prompt.md:776` — "Thinly-consumed surfaces", stamped as of v1.5.0.** Names
**two** zero-consumer surfaces:

- `makeCloseButton` (DebugLog minor 4) — both hosts that once passed it dropped it deliberately once
  Core minor 3 made the Ka0s edge the library's own default.
- `skin` (DebugLog) — same state, reached the same way.

That section is explicit that it carries consumer counts "deliberately, so that the next drift shows
up as a wrong number rather than as a heading nobody re-reads." This issue is that drift showing up.

**2. `docs/adoption/2026-08-01-v2/03_DEVIATIONS.md:634` (frozen).** Names **eight**:
`lib.FormatKV`, `lib.MAX_BUFFER`, `Sl:HelpHeader`, `Sl:HelpRows` called by name, `D:LastLine`,
`O.__pages`, the `skin` descriptor field and the `ring` descriptor field.

It also flags the interesting one: *"`HelpRows` is the notable one — every host reaches it through
`PrintHelp`, so the indented half of the row-formatter pair has no caller anywhere outside the
library, and the only textual hits in the collection are inside KickCD's own degradation stub."*
That is the whole difficulty in one sentence.

**3. A textual census run today** across the eight addons (excluding `libs/` and `tests/_kit/`) found
exactly three module-level exports with **no mention anywhere**: `DEFAULT_RING`, `FindCommand`,
`SplitVerb`.

## Why the census cannot be taken at face value, and why that is the finding

A name appearing in an addon does not mean the library's export is called. Every high-count name in
that census resolves to one of three things:

| Shape | What it means |
|---|---|
| A real call into the library | the export has a consumer |
| A **host-owned duplicate** of the same function | the convergence has not happened here |
| A **degradation stub** naming the member so a missing library cannot crash the addon | neither a call nor a duplicate |

`HelpRows` is the worked example: 15 files mention it and its consumer count is zero. Separating
these three shapes per export is the actual work this issue is asking for — a `grep` count is what
produced the disagreement above, not what resolves it.

## Why it matters

- **`-1.0` is frozen additive-only.** There is no deprecation path inside the major, so an export
  with no caller cannot be renamed or removed — it can only be worked around later. An assumption
  baked into a zero-consumer surface is permanent, and its shape is currently pinned by nothing but
  the library's own guess about what a host would want.
- **A host duplicate is the thing the convergence exists to eliminate.** The 2026-08-01 bundle already
  records the sharp case: AbsorbTracker's degraded stub reimplements `FormatRow`'s format string, "a
  second copy of the one formatter the convergence exists to eliminate."
- **No single suite covers a thinly-consumed surface.** The bundle's own reading: the Options page
  registry and the Slash schema-CLI tail "are each carried by two hosts at most, and the two hosts
  differ per surface — so no single consumer's suite covers either half, and a change to either has
  to be reasoned about rather than tested." A zero-consumer surface is that failure at its limit —
  only the library's own suite stands behind it.

## Direction

1. **Measure.** Per public export, per host, classify each textual hit as call / host duplicate /
   degradation stub. Produce today's zero-consumer set with file:line evidence, and correct
   `docs/adoption-prompt.md`'s "Thinly-consumed surfaces" counts, which are stamped v1.5.0 and are
   the file that is supposed to make drift visible.
2. **Split the result three ways.** A zero-consumer export with a host duplicate behind it is an
   **adoption** task in that host. One with no duplicate and no plausible host is a **documentation**
   task — say in the API docs that it is uncalled and why it still exists. One whose shape is
   suspect is worth settling *before* a first host adopts it, since first contact is the last moment
   the contract can be argued about.
3. **Do not delete anything.** Additive-only means the exports stay whatever the census says.

## Related

- #2 — *Decide which further modules move into LibKa0s.* Adjacent but the opposite direction: that
  issue is about moving host code **into** the library; this one is about hosts adopting what the
  library **already exports**.
- The per-addon adoption ledgers (`LIBKA0S-*`) already record several deliberate declines with
  reasons — those are answers, not gaps, and the census should not re-open them.

title: A bucket's within can name a parent absent from the record
summary: Description docs/record-schema.md introduces the per-bucket within field as the thing that makes a record self-describing — carried on each bucket "so a reader can reconstruct the nesting without the addon's source in hand". That promise does not hold when the named parent recorded no calls. Perf.Note creates a bucket lazily, on first observation ( LibKa0s/Perf.lua:411-415 ): lua local b = buckets…
full_description:
### Description

`docs/record-schema.md` introduces the per-bucket `within` field as the thing that makes a record
self-describing — carried on each bucket "so a reader can reconstruct the nesting without the
addon's source in hand". **That promise does not hold when the named parent recorded no calls.**

`Perf.Note` creates a bucket **lazily, on first observation** (`LibKa0s/Perf.lua:411-415`):

```lua
local b = buckets[key]
if not b then
  b = { calls = 0, totalMs = 0, maxMs = 0 }
  buckets[key] = b
end
```

A bucket that is declared in the descriptor but never noted during a capture therefore never enters
`buckets`, and never reaches the record — while any *child* that did fire still carries
`within = "<that parent>"`. The result is a dangling parent reference in the JSON.

**The library's own reader cannot notice.** `addBucketLines` and `addNestingNote` both fall back to
the live descriptor (`record.buckets[key].within or P.BUCKET_WITHIN[key]`, `LibKa0s/Perf.lua:214`
and `:265`), so in-process formatting stays correct. Only an **out-of-process reader of the JSON
alone** is affected — which is precisely `/wow-addon:perf-analysis` reading a frozen `dump.json`,
and precisely the case `within` was added for.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Declare two buckets where one nests in the other and the parent is not reached on every path —
   e.g. AbsorbTracker's `{ key = "appearance" }` and `{ key = "visibility", within = "appearance" }`
   (`AbsorbTracker/core/PerfSetup.lua:68` and `:72`).
2. Take an in-game capture in which the child fires and the parent does not.
3. Read the resulting `dump.json` without the addon's source in hand.

### Expected

Nesting is reconstructable from the record alone. Either the declared-but-unused parent appears with
zero counts, or the orphaned `within` is dropped from the child on the way into the record.

### Actual

In `AbsorbTracker/docs/perf-analysis/20260807-125002/dump.json`:

```jsonc
"visibility": { "calls": 21, "maxMs": 0.0915, "totalMs": 0.2388, "within": "appearance" }
```

…and `appearance` is not a key of `buckets` at all. A reader following `within` is pointed at a
parent that is not there.

### Environment

- LibKa0s **v1.13.0**, `LibKa0s-Perf-1.0` minor **7**, record `schema` **2**.
- Observed capture: AbsorbTracker 1.9.0, interface 120007, taken 2026-08-07.

**No runtime impact.** Nothing errors, nothing is lost, and no total is wrong: a parent with no calls
contributes nothing, so treating the orphaned child as top-level neither drops nor double-counts it.

### Provenance

Found while analysing [#1](https://github.com/tusharsaxena/LibKa0s/issues/1) (perf regression
thresholds), recorded in that analysis at
`Ka0sAddonsCommonTasks/docs/2026-08-24-LIBKA0S_PERF_THRESHOLDS/01_ANALYSIS.md` § 5. It did not
affect any figure in that analysis.

full_description:
**Finding `ABSORBTRACKER-A-10`** (AbsorbTracker) — from the 2026-09-07 review and standards audit remediation bundle,
`docs/2026-09-07-REVIEW_AND_STANDARDS_AUDIT_REMEDIATION/` in the Ka0sAddonsCommonTasks repo — cluster
`C12`, rule `options-ui-§13`, severity **low**. Filed by `M5-07` on LibKa0s as the kit's owner, one issue
per consumer row. Its three siblings are the other consumers: the four are `ABSORBTRACKER-A-10`,
`MULTIMETERS-A-08`, `PANELMASTER-A-07` and `PRETTYCHAT-A-10`.

### What AbsorbTracker filed

`tests/test_widgets.lua:770` — the only assertion is `assertTrue(ctx.chromeHeight > 0, ...)`; nothing asserts that the band height and the row y offsets are equal across every selection. **Remedy when the kit allows it:** a wrapping-page case asserting `chromeHeight` and each row's y offset are identical per selection, with mock heights varied so the case can fail.

### Why it is filed on LibKa0s and not on the consumer

The obstacle is the shared kit's fidelity contract, which this repository owns. `testkit/mock_base.lua`
returned 0 from `GetHeight` for every frame and defined no `SetAtlas` at all, so `OptionsWidgets.lua:433-442`'s
atlas-derived tab pitch always took its `L.TAB_H` fallback and **any `options-ui-§13` invariance assertion
passed vacuously**. Four repositories independently filed the same missing case; not one of them could write
it, and none of them could fix it either.

### What kit 15 shipped, and where it stopped

`M1-LK-08` — `24946a5` *"the shared mock can be asked how tall something is, and still answers zero by
default"* — is **purely additive**:

- `SetAtlas(name, useAtlasSize)` records what it was told and writes a height from a kit-published atlas
  table (`testkit/mock_base.lua:143-153`).
- `f:__setGeom(w, h)` is the opt-in (`:141`).
- `GetHeight` still answers zero unless geometry was armed (`:132` —
  `return (self.__geomLive and self.__geomH) or 0`).

That default is deliberate. Roughly **308 test files across ten repositories** lean on geometry answering
zero, and every assertion that passes today *because* of that flips with it. `03_SPEC.md` § `C12` puts the
flip in **kit 16** — a tag this plan does not cut — together with the cases themselves, and names flipping
`GetHeight` in kit 15 as an explicit non-goal. Kit is at `Kit.VERSION = 15` today
(`testkit/framework.lua:20`).

### So this row is deferred, not fixed

`05_TRACEABILITY.md` Part 4 says it plainly: after this plan the four findings are still open, with the
obstacle removed, and **no work item in this plan writes a tab-strip geometry case in any of the four
repositories**. The rows are marked `deferred` rather than `fix` for exactly that reason. What covers the
interval is an operator: `06_SMOKE_TESTS.md` § 3.5 cycles every multi-tab panel in all nine addons after the
`M4-01` wave — a weaker check than the four findings ask for, named rather than left unstated.

### What closes it

Kit 16: `GetHeight` returns recorded geometry by default, once each consumer has adopted the opt-in where it
needs it. Then the consumer above carries a case asserting the chrome band height and every row's y offset
are identical across each tab selection, **verified red** under a mutation to the tab atlas heights. A green
case written before the flip proves nothing, which is the whole reason this is parked instead of closed.

it, and none of them could fix it either.

### What kit 15 shipped, and where it stopped

`M1-LK-08` — `24946a5` *"the shared mock can be asked how tall something is, and still answers zero by
default"* — is **purely additive**:

- `SetAtlas(name, useAtlasSize)` records what it was told and writes a height from a kit-published atlas
  table (`testkit/mock_base.lua:143-153`).
- `f:__setGeom(w, h)` is the opt-in (`:141`).
- `GetHeight` still answers zero unless geometry was armed (`:132` —
  `return (self.__geomLive and self.__geomH) or 0`).

That default is deliberate. Roughly **308 test files across ten repositories** lean on geometry answering
zero, and every assertion that passes today *because* of that flips with it. `03_SPEC.md` § `C12` puts the
flip in **kit 16** — a tag this plan does not cut — together with the cases themselves, and names flipping
`GetHeight` in kit 15 as an explicit non-goal. Kit is at `Kit.VERSION = 15` today
(`testkit/framework.lua:20`).

### So this row is deferred, not fixed

`05_TRACEABILITY.md` Part 4 says it plainly: after this plan the four findings are still open, with the
obstacle removed, and **no work item in this plan writes a tab-strip geometry case in any of the four
repositories**. The rows are marked `deferred` rather than `fix` for exactly that reason. What covers the
interval is an operator: `06_SMOKE_TESTS.md` § 3.5 cycles every multi-tab panel in all nine addons after the
`M4-01` wave — a weaker check than the four findings ask for, named rather than left unstated.

### What closes it

Kit 16: `GetHeight` returns recorded geometry by default, once each consumer has adopted the opt-in where it
needs it. Then the consumer above carries a case asserting the chrome band height and every row's y offset
are identical across each tab selection, **verified red** under a mutation to the tab atlas heights. A green
case written before the flip proves nothing, which is the whole reason this is parked instead of closed.

summary: Ship more than one set of class, role and spec icons and let the player pick which set a window uses. Reference points - Details! is the benchmark: several icon packs, selectable per display, which is one of the reasons its windows can be made to match wildly different UIs. - EllesmereUI Damage Meters takes the opposite approach — one set, chosen to match the rest of the EllesmereUI suite — which …
full_description:
Ship more than one set of class, role and spec icons and let the player pick which set a window uses.

### Reference points

- **Details!** is the benchmark: several icon packs, selectable per display, which is one of the reasons its windows can be made to match wildly different UIs.
- **EllesmereUI Damage Meters** takes the opposite approach — one set, chosen to match the rest of the EllesmereUI suite — which is worth noting because a player running a full UI suite wants the meter to disappear into it rather than assert its own style.
- **Scoot** uses the client's own class and spec art.

### Notes for whoever picks this up

- The data these icons key off is **NeverSecret and therefore always available mid-pull**: `classFilename`, `specIconID` and the roster's role all keep working at the height of a pull when every number on the row is opaque. That is exactly why the row's identity is carried by icons and the name rather than by its numbers — see `docs/data-flow.md` §7 and `modules/Row.lua`'s `drawClassIcon` / `drawSpecIcon` / `drawRoleIcon`.
- **`specIconID` is a file id the game hands us**, not a name we choose. A custom spec set therefore needs its own id→art mapping, and a spec the map does not cover has to fall back to the client's icon rather than draw nothing.
- Roles are the easy third: there are four values (`TANK`, `HEALER`, `DAMAGER`, `NONE`) and the last one must be drawable, since a follower NPC or an ungrouped player legitimately has no role.
- A set is media, so it lands in LibSharedMedia the same way the console font does (`core/LSMPatch.lua`) — which means the same licence and registry-key questions as #4 and the custom-glyph issue, times however many sets ship.
- The selection is a schema row (`window.icons.*` already exists as a group), so the panel, `/mm set` and the per-page reset all come from one place.
- Worth confirming a set covers every class **before** it ships: a missing class is invisible until somebody in that class joins your group.

full_description:
When a key or a dungeon finishes, put up a summary of the run — not the live window, a deliberate end-of-run panel — after a short configurable delay.

### Reference points

- **EllesmereUI Damage Meters** already hooks the event this needs: `EllesmereUIDamageMeters.lua:687` registers `CHALLENGE_MODE_COMPLETED`, and the handler at line 712 uses it to auto-swap a window from `Current` to `Overall` on key completion (`autoSwapMythic`). That swap is a smaller version of the same idea: at the end of a key, what the player wants to look at changes.
- **Details!** ships an end-of-encounter breakdown players go and open; the difference asked for here is that it arrives on its own.
- **Scoot** has no equivalent.

### Notes for whoever picks this up

- **The delay is the whole feature, not a nicety.** At the instant a key completes the player is being shown Blizzard's own completion UI, loot is rolling, and the group is moving. A summary that lands in that moment is noise. It also has a technical reason: the Overall session's totals settle a moment after completion, so a panel drawn immediately can show a number that changes under it.
- `CHALLENGE_MODE_COMPLETED` is the M+ event. A non-keyed dungeon needs a different trigger — worth deciding whether this is M+ only (simpler, and where the demand is) or every instance.
- **`core/MythicMeters.lua` is the addon's single game-event listener** and it must stay that way (architecture-§4): register there, translate, publish onto the bus, and let a module decide what to do. Do not register an event inside a module.
- By the time this fires, combat is over and the restriction has lifted, so the values are plain and everything the live grid cannot do — sorting by value, percentages, arithmetic — is legal here. That makes the summary panel a genuinely richer view than the window, not a screenshot of it.
- A dismissed popup must stay dismissed for that run, and the delay wants a schema row rather than a constant.
- Pairs with the automatic-screenshot issue: the screenshot is only worth taking once this panel is on screen.

full_description:
Optionally take a screenshot automatically once the end-of-run summary is up, so a player has a record of the run without having to remember to press the key.

Depends on the end-of-dungeon popup issue — there is nothing worth photographing until that panel exists.

### Reference points

- **Details!** is the closest prior art: players habitually screenshot its end-of-fight breakdown, which is exactly why doing it for them is worth something.
- Neither **EllesmereUI Damage Meters** nor **Scoot** does this today, so there is no implementation to copy — only the behaviour to get right.

### Notes for whoever picks this up

- `Screenshot()` is the API. The trap is timing: it captures the frame as it is **at the moment it is called**, so calling it in the same frame the popup is created photographs a panel that has not drawn yet. It needs to happen a frame or two after the panel is up, not on the same tick.
- It captures the **whole screen**, including whatever else is on it. That is a reason to fire it while the summary is the thing worth looking at, and a reason it must be **off by default and explicitly opt-in** — an addon that silently writes files to a player's disk is not a thing to ship on by default.
- Screenshots land in the client's own `Screenshots/` folder; the addon cannot name, move or read them. Say that plainly in the setting's description rather than implying more control than exists.
- Interacts with the player's own UI-hiding habits: consider whether to hide the addon's other windows first, and whether that is a setting or a decision.
- One screenshot per run, not one per attempt — and if the popup is dismissed before the delay elapses, no screenshot.

full_description:
When a window is dragged near another Mythic Meters window — or near a screen edge — snap it flush rather than leaving a two-pixel gap nobody can fix by hand.

### Reference points

- **Details!** snaps its windows to one another and keeps them attached, which is how a player ends up with a damage window and a healing window that behave as one block.
- **EllesmereUI Damage Meters** relies on its suite's shared positioning instead — worth knowing as the alternative philosophy: a UI suite can put things in the right place because it owns the whole screen; a standalone meter cannot, so it has to make manual placement cheap.
- **Scoot** pixel-snaps its *borders* (`core/borders.lua:104-107`, `SetSnapToPixelGrid`) — a different problem, but the same instinct that a two-pixel misalignment is what makes a UI look homemade.

### Notes for whoever picks this up

- **This one runs straight into rule R3 and needs care.** A frame handed a secret meter value has secret anchoring and position data, and that propagates to anything anchored to it — so this addon may not ask a live window where it is. `docs/data-flow.md` §7 is the rule.
- **The escape hatch already exists and this feature should be built entirely on it.** Every window keeps `inst.anchor`: a bare, empty, invisible frame parented to `UIParent` with no children, no textures and no cells, which the visible window is anchored to. It never holds a value, so `GetPoint` / `GetWidth` on the anchor are legal — and drag and resize already act on it. Snapping is anchor-to-anchor geometry, and if it is written against anchors it is safe by construction.
- `SaveSize` goes one step further and takes the size from the arguments `OnSizeChanged` was handed rather than from a getter. Worth matching that discipline.
- Positions are stored in config (`frame.position`) and never read back off the visible frame — the snapped result has to be written there, or it will not survive a reload.
- Decide whether a snap is *sticky* (the two windows move together afterwards, as Details! does) or a one-time alignment on drop. Sticky is a relationship that has to be stored, invalidated when either window is deleted, and survive a profile switch; alignment-on-drop is nearly free. They are very different amounts of work and the issue should be split if sticky is wanted.
- Screen-edge snapping needs `UIParent`'s dimensions and the window's own scale — both legal to read, neither on a value-bearing frame.

title: Keep snapped windows attached, so they move as one block
summary: Stage 2 of 11. Once two windows have been snapped flush, keep them attached: moving one moves the other, so a damage window and a healing window behave as a single block. Description 11 covers one-time alignment on drop — snap flush on release, write the result to frame.position , done. This issue is the other half of that decision: the sticky relationship that survives the drop. Split out because…
full_description:
Stage 2 of #11. Once two windows have been snapped flush, keep them attached: moving one moves the other, so a damage window and a healing window behave as a single block.

### Description

#11 covers one-time alignment on drop — snap flush on release, write the result to `frame.position`, done. This issue is the other half of that decision: the *sticky* relationship that survives the drop.

Split out because the two are very different amounts of work. Alignment-on-drop is nearly free; a stored attachment is a relationship with a lifecycle, and folding it into #11 would hide that.

### Motivation

**Details!** attaches its windows to one another and keeps them attached, which is how a player ends up with a damage window and a healing window that move as one object rather than two things that have to be re-aligned every time either is nudged.

**EllesmereUI Damage Meters** relies on its suite's shared positioning instead — worth knowing as the alternative philosophy: a UI suite can put things in the right place because it owns the whole screen; a standalone meter cannot, so it has to make manual placement cheap.

### Proposed behavior

- After a snap, the two windows are recorded as attached, and dragging either one carries the other.
- The relationship is stored in config, so it survives a reload.
- It is invalidated when either window is deleted.
- It survives a profile switch — or is deliberately dropped on one; that decision is _TBD_.
- Whether attachment is strictly pairwise or chains across three or more windows is _TBD_.

### Acceptance criteria

- **Rule R3 is not violated.** All geometry comes from `inst.anchor` — the bare, empty, invisible `UIParent`-parented frame with no children, no textures and no cells, which never holds a meter value and is therefore legal to call `GetPoint` / `GetWidth` on. The visible window is never asked where it is. See `docs/data-flow.md` §7.
- Sizing follows `SaveSize`'s existing discipline: take the size from the arguments `OnSizeChanged` was handed, not from a getter.
- Attachment state is written to config and never read back off a frame; positions still round-trip through `frame.position`.
- Deleting one window of an attached pair leaves the other in a valid state, with no dangling reference.
- Behaviour across a profile switch matches whatever is decided for the _TBD_ above, and is covered by the headless suite where it can be.

full_description:
**Status:** triaged — decided, not now. Raised 2026-08-22 after being **built and removed** the same
day. This issue exists so a fourth attempt starts from the measurements rather than from the idea.

## What was wanted

A third **Death timestamps** style, beside *Time of day* and *How long ago*: how far into the run or
the fight a death happened, rendered `mm:ss`. Requested during the issue #1 work, shipped, and never
worked — it always rendered identically to *Time of day*.

## Why it does not work today

Nothing on the 12.x client can date a past death against the run it happened in. Four derivations
were built; every one failed, and the failures are measurements rather than opinions. All were
captured with `/mm debug recap` on a live client, reviewing a finished key from outside the dungeon.

| Derivation | Result |
|---|---|
| The Deaths source row's own `deathTimeSeconds` | **`-1` on the Overall session** — for all eighteen deaths in the capture. Overall is what a window shows by default. |
| Join to the **Current** session on `deathRecapID` | Current carries real offsets *during* a run (1017–1434s in an earlier capture) and held **zero rows** once the run was over — which is exactly when a death list gets read. |
| `time() - C_DamageMeter.GetSessionDurationSeconds(...)` | The session duration is **combat time, not wall time**: ~32 minutes of it spanning a run whose deaths were ~175 minutes earlier. `now - duration` lands nowhere near the run's start. |
| An anchor the addon stamps itself, on `DAMAGE_METER_RESET` | Built (`State.segmentStartedAt` + `Provider.SegmentOffset`) and still did not produce a usable figure in front of a live client. Removed with the rest. |

The verbatim capture that settled it:

```
-- deaths, Current -- 0 rows, reason=nil
-- deaths, Overall -- 18 rows
  [ 1] name=Boogie-Muradin  deathTime=-1  recap=19
  ...
-- dating --
  window 1: sessionType=0  text.deathTimeFormat=elapsed
  id=19  row deathTimeSeconds=-1  DeathOffset(id)=nil
    clock=19:16:40  ago=175m ago  elapsed=19:16:40
```

## What IS available, and is worth building on

* **Every death carries an absolute epoch timestamp** on its recap's newest event
  (`C_DeathRecap.GetRecapEvents(id)[1].timestamp`). That is what the two surviving styles use, and it
  is always present. Deaths can therefore be dated *relative to each other* with no client support
  at all.
* Recap ids are **session-scoped counters**, identical across Current and Overall in the same order.
* `deathTimeSeconds` is real on **Current, while a run is live**. A style that only claimed to work
  during a run would be honest and would need no new API.

## Plausible ways in, for whoever picks this up

1. **Anchor on the first death of the session.** Needs nothing new: subtract the oldest death's
   timestamp from each. It is *not* "time into the fight" and must not be labelled as though it were
   — "time since the first death" is what it would be, and that may be useful enough on its own.
2. **Restrict the style to a live run**, reading `deathTimeSeconds` off Current and saying plainly in
   the setting's description that it is blank afterwards.
3. **`C_ChallengeMode` / `GetWorldElapsedTime`** for keys specifically, accepting that it answers
   nothing outside one. Not investigated — worth a probe before any code.
4. **Dump `C_DamageMeter.GetAvailableCombatSessions()`.** Its shape has never been inspected and it
   is the one plausible source of a session start time still unexamined. **Do this first** — it is
   one line in the probe and could make the whole issue trivial.

## The method note, which is the real content here

Three fixes shipped before the removal. Each was plausible from a screenshot, each had passing unit
tests, and none of the offline fixtures reproduced the live client. What ended it was
`/mm debug recap` growing a **dating** section that prints the *inputs* — the row's own figure, each
lookup's answer, and every style side by side — instead of the conclusion. The first miss should
have triggered that, not the third.

**`/mm debug recap`'s dating section is deliberately kept in the codebase** even though the feature
it was written for is gone, and its comment says why. Run it before writing any code here.

## Commits

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| `5ddd79a` | Added the style and the `Death timestamps` setting |
| `2c6c35d` | First fix — the Current-session lookup (`Provider.DeathOffset`) |
| `7d203dc` | Added the `-- dating --` probe rather than guessing a third time |
| `98130f4` | Second fix — the addon's own segment anchor (`State.segmentStartedAt`) |
| `9451436` | **Removal.** Reverses all of the above; keeps the probe |

Reversal is also recorded as §11 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-22-death-recap-design.md`, and
as a bullet under **Known limitations** in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.

Severity **low**: the two remaining timestamp styles cover the common questions, and nothing is
broken by its absence.

full_description:
**Finding (owner's in-client diagnostics, 2026-09-26).** After fighting a PvP Training Dummy, `/mm diagnostics` reported `enemies carrying a player class: 1 of 1` — `[1] name=PvP Training Dummy guid=plain creatureID=243211 display=0 class=WARRIOR`. So an NPC can carry a `RAID_CLASS_COLORS` class filename, and the client files the enemy column's sources under display type None (0), not Enemy (2).

**Why it matters.** The aggregator's companion rule (`modules/Aggregator.lua`, around :751-766: a None source with a player class is admitted as a companion) is now the only thing that would stop a mob from reaching a grid column, and it would admit a classed mob. `isEnemySource` (around :721-724) keys on Enemy (2), which never arrives, and identity mode (`modules/Aggregator_Identity.lua` around :255 and :631) relies on it alone.

**Nothing is wrong in practice today.** In the same session the grid showed only the player (DamageDone had one source); mobs have never been seen in the ally meter types. This is hardening.

**Fix direction.** Tighten the None admission, for example require a Player-style GUID or a known companion creature ID (careful: Valeera's GUID is `Creature-…`, see `tests/test_aggregator.lua` around :786), and decide whether to keep or retire the Enemy gate. Tests first: a classed NPC source in DamageDone is refused; a companion is still admitted.

Background: MultiMeters c374876 (diagnostics now report the class count), docs/midnight-quirks.md "Enemies are filed under None, not Enemy".

**Finding (2026-09-26).** #1 was closed as done on 2026-08-22 with a death-recap drill-down (merge 8ab2c32, plus 87cacc8, fda8ba2, 2291067), not the full two-pane window with an event-by-event breakdown. 2. **Or retire the idea:** reword the diagnostic so it no longer refers to #1, and fix the false-positive counting so a future verdict is trustworthy.

title: Add an optional text label inside a panel
summary: Description Panels are anonymous blocks today. Add an optional text label drawn inside a panel, styled and positioned independently of the panel itself. The accent bar is the shape to copy: it is already a self-contained optional decoration with its own enable switch, media selection, colour (with a class-colour flag), thickness and offset — and it costs the CLI, the settings page and the field du…
full_description:
### Description

Panels are anonymous blocks today. Add an optional text label drawn inside a panel,
styled and positioned independently of the panel itself.

The accent bar is the shape to copy: it is already a self-contained optional
decoration with its own enable switch, media selection, colour (with a class-colour
flag), thickness and offset — and it costs the CLI, the settings page and the field
dump nothing extra, because it flows through `PANEL_TEMPLATE` / `PANEL_FIELD_TYPE` /
`PANEL_FIELD_ORDER` like everything else.

### Motivation

- The addon's own tagline is that a screen of separate frames should read as "a few
  deliberate groups". Those groups are currently unnamed.
- Unlock mode already demonstrates the value — it draws a centred gold name label so a
  near-invisible panel can be found and grabbed. That label is temporary and
  unstyleable; users will want a permanent one they control.
- The seams already exist. `C.COLOR_FIELDS` makes class-colour a one-row addition,
  LibSharedMedia is wired through `Compat.FetchMedia`, and any field added to the three
  constants tables gets CLI coercion, `/pm panel <name>` output, copy-settings and
  profile support with no per-field work.

### Proposed behavior

From the request:

| Field | Type | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `labelFont` | media (`font`) | New LSM media type — the addon uses `background`, `border` and `statusbar` today, not `font`. Needs a `C.MEDIA_FALLBACK` entry. |
| `labelFontSize` | number | Named min/max in `core/Constants.lua`. |
| `labelOutline` | enum | `NONE` / `OUTLINE` / `THICKOUTLINE`. |
| `labelColor` | color | |
| `labelClassColor` | boolean | One new row in `C.COLOR_FIELDS`; nothing else changes. |
| `labelPoint` | point | Reuses the existing nine-point `C.POINTS` list. |
| `labelX` / `labelY` | number | Offsets from that anchor. |

Discovered while reading the current field set — not in the original ask:

| Field | Type | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `labelEnabled` | boolean | Mirrors `accentEnabled`. "No label" should be the switch, not an empty string. |
| `labelText` | string | The text itself. Only `name` is a string field today. |
| `labelMonochrome` | boolean | WoW font flags are a comma list; `MONOCHROME` is orthogonal to outline and reads badly folded into the same dropdown. |
| `labelJustifyH` / `labelJustifyV` | enum | Distinct from the anchor point once the text wraps or a max width is set. |
| `labelShadowColor` / `labelShadowOffset` | color / number | `FontString` supports both; cheap legibility win over a busy background. |
| `labelMaxWidth`, `labelWordWrap` | number / boolean | What happens when the text is wider than the panel. |
| `labelAlpha` | number | Or inherit the panel's `alpha` — see open questions. |
| `labelDrawLayer` / sublevel | enum / number | The text must land above the accent bar and the background, not behind them. |

### Acceptance criteria

- New fields live in `PANEL_TEMPLATE`, `PANEL_FIELD_TYPE` and `PANEL_FIELD_ORDER`, so
  the CLI, `/pm panel <name>`, copy-settings and profiles pick them up with no
  per-field edit.
- Class colour is one new row in `C.COLOR_FIELDS` — not re-decided at any call site.
- Every bound is a named constant in `core/Constants.lua`, never inlined
  (`options-ui-§8`).
- Purely additive to the record and filled by `Registry.Sanitize` from the template, so
  `NS.SCHEMA_VERSION` does not move and no migration is needed.
- The label must not make the panel mouse-interactive — panels are click-through and
  stay that way.
- The panel editor gains a Label section that refreshes in place on `MSG_PANEL` like
  every other scalar (`options-ui-§11`).
- README and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` updated; tests cover the new fields; green gate
  (`lua tests/run.lua`, `luacheck .` at 0/0).

### Open questions

- Default `labelText` — empty, or the panel's own name?
- How does a user label interact with unlock mode's gold centre label? Suppress one,
  offset them, or let them overlap?
- Multi-word text from the CLI. Panel names are addressed by first word only today
  (accepted deviation A-008), so `/pm panel Chat labelText Damage Meter` needs a
  decision on quoting.
- Truncation vs. wrap vs. overflow when the text is wider than the panel.
- Is the `FontString` part of the public anchor contract, i.e. does it get a
  deterministic global name like `PanelMaster_Panel_<slug>_Label`?
- Dynamic tokens (spec name, character name) — probably out of scope, recording it so
  the field shape does not accidentally preclude it.

A per-frame write through Registry:Set would broadcast MS…
full_description:
### Description

The panel editor's sliders commit on `OnMouseUp` only, so a panel does not follow its Width, Height,
X or Y slider while that slider is being dragged. You set a value, release, and only then see the
result.

### Motivation

This is deliberate, not an oversight — recorded in `docs/reviews/2026-07-30/05_FINAL_SUMMARY.md` ▸
Known follow-ups. A per-frame write through `Registry:Set` would broadcast `MSG_PANEL` on every
frame of the drag, and every subscriber would repaint at that rate.

It is still the weakest part of the editing experience: sizing a panel by feel means release, look,
grab, adjust, release, look.

### Proposed behavior

A throttled preview path that moves or resizes the *frame* directly during the drag without going
through the registry, then does exactly one real `Registry:Set` on `OnMouseUp`. The frame is the
thing the user is looking at; the record only has to be right when they let go.

_TBD_: the throttle interval, and whether the preview path needs to be reverted if the drag is
cancelled rather than released.

### Acceptance criteria

- Dragging a geometry slider moves the panel live.
- Exactly one `Registry:Set` and one `MSG_PANEL` per drag gesture, on release.
- No repaint storm: the drag does not broadcast on the bus at all until it ends.
- Green gate: `lua tests/run.lua`, `luacheck .` at 0/0.

title: Animate the mouseover fade instead of snapping
summary: Description The mouseover fade snaps between its two alpha values instead of animating between them. From docs/ARCHITECTURE.md ▸ Known limitations: The mouseover fade is a hard cut, not a smooth fade. Alpha snaps between the two values at the 10Hz poll. An animated transition is a natural refinement. Motivation This is the only entry in that list that proposes its own fix rather than justifying th…
full_description:
### Description

The mouseover fade snaps between its two alpha values instead of animating between them.

From `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` ▸ Known limitations:

> The mouseover fade is a hard cut, not a smooth fade. Alpha snaps between the two values at the 10Hz
> poll. An animated transition is a natural refinement.

### Motivation

This is the only entry in that list that proposes its own fix rather than justifying the status quo.
A panel set to `mouseoverAlpha 0` currently pops in and out of existence as the cursor crosses it,
which reads as a glitch rather than a reveal — and the feature's whole purpose is to keep a panel
unobtrusive until wanted.

### Proposed behavior

Interpolate alpha across the existing shared 10Hz ticker rather than setting it in one step. The
ticker is already there and already walks every tracked panel, so this is a change to what happens
per tick, not new machinery.

_TBD_: the transition duration, and whether fade-in and fade-out should differ (a fast reveal with a
slower fade-out is the usual choice).

### Constraints

- The ticker is the addon's only per-frame-ish path. It must stay allocation-free and must not gain a
  debug call (`anti-patterns` #43).
- A panel whose mouseover state changes mid-transition has to reverse cleanly, not restart.
- The visual result cannot be verified headlessly — the harness can assert the alpha sequence, not
  that it looks right, so this needs an in-client check.

### Acceptance criteria

- Alpha moves smoothly between `alpha` and `mouseoverAlpha` in both directions.
- No additional timer: the existing shared ticker does the work.
- Reversing mid-transition does not jump.
- Green gate: `lua tests/run.lua`, `luacheck .` at 0/0.

title: Ship bundled artwork as optional download packs to cut download size

full_description:
### Description

Stop shipping every bundled artwork to every player. Split the catalog's assets into **optional
art packs** — separate downloads, each a companion addon folder that appends its own rows to the
catalog when installed — so a player who wants the Factions art downloads the Factions art and
nobody carries the rest.

This issue originally proposed `## LoadOnDemand: 1` sub-addons loaded via `LoadAddOn` on first use.
That framing is wrong, and the section below records why so it is not re-litigated.

### The load-on-demand question, settled

The premise was that bundled art is unconditionally *resident* and that deferring it would cut the
runtime footprint. It is not, and it would not:

- **WoW's load-on-demand unit is an addon folder, and it governs Lua/XML only.** `LoadOnDemand` +
  `LoadAddOn` decide when a folder's *scripts* execute. There is no per-file LoD for media, and no
  API that defers or unloads one texture.
- **Textures are never listed in the TOC and are never "loaded" by the addon.** The client reads a
  `.tga` off disk at the moment a `Texture:SetTexture(path)` actually draws it, and manages its own
  cache and eviction afterwards. Per-artwork on-demand loading is therefore *already the behavior*,
  for free, with no packs, no `LoadAddOn` and no code.
- **This addon already relies on that.** `rec.artCustomPath` renders a user's arbitrary file that no
  TOC has ever heard of (`modules/Artwork.lua:118-124`). If a TOC entry were required for a texture
  to load, the Custom path feature could not work at all.
- **So the only unconditionally-resident thing is the Lua catalog** — today four rows of eight
  fields. Deferring *that* at per-artwork granularity would mean one addon folder, one TOC and one
  `LoadAddOn` call per image, each one appearing in the player's AddOns list, to postpone a few
  hundred bytes of table. Strictly worse than doing nothing.
- The measurement this issue previously asked for cannot even see the thing it was meant to weigh:
  `GetAddOnMemoryUsage` reports Lua allocation only. Texture memory is never attributed to an addon.

**Conclusion: there is no runtime footprint win available here.** What survives is the cost the
`.pkgmeta` comments were already reasoning about — bytes shipped and bytes on disk.

### Motivation, restated honestly

Every asset is a 512×512 32-bit TGA at ~1 MB. Every motif ships as a `-bw` / `-color` pair. The
catalog is heading for several categories (`C.ARTWORK_CATEGORIES` declares General, Races, Classes,
Expansions, Factions). That is tens of megabytes downloaded and kept on disk by every player, the
overwhelming majority of whom will enable art on a handful of panels.

Adding art is deliberately cheap — "one row here plus a `.tga` file, and no code change anywhere
else" (`modules/Artwork.lua:21-22`). That property is worth keeping, and it is exactly what makes
the unconditional download grow with every contribution with nothing pushing back.

`.pkgmeta` already excludes `media/artwork/raw` on precisely this reasoning: don't ship megabytes
the client cannot use. Packs extend it to art the client *can* use but the player never asked for.

### Proposed behavior

Split at the **packaging** boundary, not the loading boundary.

- The main addon ships a small core set only.
- Each additional category ships as its own download: a companion addon folder
  (`PanelMaster_Art<Category>`) containing `media/artwork/` plus one small Lua that registers its
  rows. A **normal, always-loaded** addon — no `LoadOnDemand`, no `LoadAddOn`. Its Lua is a few
  hundred bytes; there is nothing left worth deferring.
- `## Dependencies: PanelMaster` on the companion TOC, so it loads after the main addon and refuses
  to load without it.
- **A companion cannot reach `NS`.** `local addonName, NS = ...` is PanelMaster's private per-addon
  namespace; a separate addon folder has no access to it. This needs a small **public registration
  API** on the main addon — the one genuinely new piece of code here. `Artwork.Entry`'s linear scan
  already exists to permit exactly this ("an index would go stale the moment anything appended to
  `Artwork.Catalog` at runtime — which is precisely the extension path this table exists to offer",
  `modules/Artwork.lua:90-93`), so registration is an append plus validation, not a redesign.
- Registration must validate what it appends — id, `file`, positive `w`/`h` — and skip a bad row
  rather than let a third-party pack push a division-by-zero into `BuildArtSpec`.
- `Artwork.List`, `Artwork.Entry`, `BuildArtSpec` and the editor dropdown need **no change**: they
  read whatever is in `Artwork.Catalog`.
- `id` remains the saved-variables contract. A player who uninstalls a pack degrades to "this panel
  draws no artwork" through the existing unknown-id path in `resolve()` — no error, no profile
  corruption, and the art returns if they reinstall.

### Explicitly not doing

- `LoadOnDemand` sub-addons, `LoadAddOn` calls, a lazy per-category load triggered by the dropdown.
- A split catalog index with a `pack` owner field per row.

All rejected on the evidence above, not on effort.

### Notes

- Multi-folder packaging is a **new structural pattern for this addon**, and the Ka0s WoW Addon
  Standard defines the layout for a single-addon tree. Check the standard before implementing; if
  it has no answer, raise it upstream or record it as an accepted deviation.
- Needs `.pkgmeta` work to emit more than one artifact, and a decision about whether packs are
  separate distribution projects or one optional bundle.
- Interacts with `tools/artwork/import.py`, which writes to a single `media/artwork/` today and
  would need a pack destination.
- The public registration API is shared with #11 (user-supplied artwork via a companion folder);
  whichever lands first should build it, and the other should consume it unchanged. Neither issue
  blocks the other.

title: Let players supply their own artwork via a companion addon folder
summary: Description A MyMedia-style route for player-authored art: a companion addon folder the player owns, into which they drop their own images, which then appear in the artwork dropdown as first-class catalog entries — label, category, correct native size, tint behavior — instead of a hand-typed path. The pattern is LibSharedMedia's SharedMedia_MyMedia : the library ships its own media, and a separate…
full_description:
### Description

A MyMedia-style route for player-authored art: a companion addon folder the player owns, into which
they drop their own images, which then appear in the artwork dropdown as first-class catalog
entries — label, category, correct native size, tint behavior — instead of a hand-typed path.

The pattern is LibSharedMedia's `SharedMedia_MyMedia`: the library ships its own media, and a
separate, user-owned folder registers more. The key property is that it is a **separate addon
folder**. Anything a player drops inside `PanelMaster/media/artwork/` is destroyed by the next
addon update, so user art cannot live there.

Today the only route is the reserved **Custom path…** entry, and it is thin by design
(`modules/Artwork.lua:118-124`): the player types a full `Interface\AddOns\…\file.tga` per panel,
gets no dropdown entry, no label, no category, and — because there is no catalog row — no declared
dimensions. `Artwork.CUSTOM_NATIVE_SIZE` assumes 256, so `STATIC`, `FIT` and `TILE` are wrong for
any 512×512 art the player actually produces (`modules/Artwork.lua:78-84`). It is an escape hatch,
not a way to add art.

### Motivation

- The bundled catalog can never cover what players want — guild crests, personal sigils, motifs for
  a specific UI theme.
- `docs/artwork-spec.md` already documents exactly how to author a conforming asset and already
  carries a generation brief for an image model. The knowledge exists; there is no path for a
  non-developer to *use* it.
- `tools/artwork/import.py` already performs the conversion that makes a generated plate usable
  (luminance-to-alpha, chroma key, power-of-two letterboxing, margin checks). It is developer-only
  and repo-only today.
- `Artwork.Entry` is a linear scan specifically so rows can be appended at runtime — "precisely the
  extension path this table exists to offer" (`modules/Artwork.lua:90-93`). The addon was built
  anticipating this.

### Proposed behavior

**1. Authoring instructions for players**

- A player-facing condensation of `docs/artwork-spec.md`, shipped as `README.txt` inside the
  companion folder: the hard requirements (32-bit TGA, power-of-two, transparent background, 2–4 px
  margin), and the tintable vs. full-color choice in plain terms.
- Copy-paste generation prompts, including the white-on-black route already documented in the spec
  ("Most image models cannot emit a real alpha channel") and the magenta-backdrop route for color
  art, so the output lands in a form `import.py` can convert.

**2. A companion kit under `tools/myart/`**

- `setup.bat` — creates `PanelMaster_MyArt/` alongside `PanelMaster/` in `Interface/AddOns/`, with
  `raw/` (drop zone), `media/` (converted output), a TOC, and `README.txt`.
- `README.txt` — tells the player where to put source images and what to run next.
- `import.bat` — runs `tools/artwork/import.py` over everything in `raw/`, writing `.tga` into
  `media/`.
- The same script regenerates `PanelMaster_MyArt/Catalog.lua` — one row per converted asset — and
  the TOC file list, so the addon picks the art up on next reload.

**3. Registration**

- A companion addon **cannot reach `NS`**: `local addonName, NS = ...` is PanelMaster's private
  per-addon namespace. This needs a small **public registration API** on the main addon, which
  validates each submitted row (id, `file`, positive `w`/`h`) and skips a bad one rather than
  letting a third-party file push a division by zero into `BuildArtSpec`.
- The companion TOC carries `## Dependencies: PanelMaster` for load order.
- `Artwork.List`, `Artwork.Entry`, `BuildArtSpec` and the editor dropdown need no change.

**Relationship to #10 — no dependency.** #10's load-on-demand premise was evaluated and dropped:
textures are never listed in a TOC and are loaded by the client on `SetTexture`, so per-artwork
on-demand loading already happens for free. Nothing here waits on it. The one shared piece is the
public registration API above, which both issues need; whichever lands first builds it.

### Acceptance criteria

- A player who has never opened a Lua file can run one `.bat`, drop a PNG in a folder, run a second
  `.bat`, and see their art in the artwork dropdown with a readable label after `/reload`.
- Art added this way survives a PanelMaster update.
- Uninstalling or emptying the companion folder degrades affected panels to "no artwork" through the
  existing unknown-id path — no error, no profile corruption.
- A malformed or hand-edited companion catalog cannot error the main addon.
- Player art is credited to the player, not to the bundled catalog's credit line.

**Open questions**

- **Python/Pillow dependency.** `import.bat` inherits it. Options: detect and report it cleanly with
  an install link; ship a prebuilt converter; or drop conversion entirely and instruct players to
  export 32-bit TGA from any image editor (zero dependency, more work for the player, no
  luminance-to-alpha help). _TBD_ — worth deciding before building.
- **Windows only.** `.bat` leaves macOS/Linux players with nothing. Sibling `.sh`, or accepted? _TBD_
- **Packaging.** `.pkgmeta` currently ignores `tools/`, so the kit would not reach players at all.
  Needs resolving — the kit is the deliverable *for* players. _TBD_
- **Id collisions.** `Artwork.Entry` returns the first match, so a player id equal to a bundled id
  would be silently shadowed. Namespace player ids, or reject collisions? _TBD_

title: Autosize a panel to a target frame, with per-side padding

Motivation Today a panel is sized by hand ( width / height , clamped to C.MIN_SIZE / C.MAX_SIZE ) a…
full_description:
### Description

Let a panel derive its size from a target frame instead of being given a fixed
`width`/`height`. The panel would track the target frame's size, plus a configurable
amount of extra spacing, so the panel reads as a backdrop *around* that frame rather
than a rectangle the user has to hand-fit.

### Motivation

Today a panel is sized by hand (`width`/`height`, clamped to `C.MIN_SIZE`/`C.MAX_SIZE`)
and positioned by hand (`point`/`x`/`y`). Backing a specific frame therefore means
eyeballing the numbers, and re-eyeballing them whenever that frame changes size.

### Proposed behavior

- A panel can name a **target frame** to size against.
- Extra spacing beyond the target's bounds is configurable as **+x** and **+y**.
- Spacing has a **direction** — up / down / left / right — so the padding can be
  applied asymmetrically rather than only being split evenly on both axes.
- _TBD_: whether autosize also implies auto-position (anchoring to the target), or
  only drives width/height while `point`/`x`/`y` stay manual.
- _TBD_: how the target frame is chosen (typed frame name, mouseover picker, both).
- _TBD_: behavior when the target frame does not exist, is hidden, or resizes at runtime.

### Acceptance criteria

- A panel set to autosize matches its target frame's size plus the configured +x / +y
  spacing, in the configured direction(s).
- The setting is reachable from both the panel editor and the `/pm panel` slash surface,
  consistent with the existing `width` / `height` fields.
- _TBD_: remaining criteria pending the open questions above.

full_description:
Owner's option (a) for the `architecture-§5` register row in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` ▸ Documented deviations (the fields on a panel), recorded from audit finding PanelMaster-A-07 (audit PM-039). The row was re-decided as **keep** (option b) on 2026-09-24; this issue holds the adopt path so the decision can be revisited.

## Background

LibKa0s-Schema-1.0 has forwarded an instance id since Schema minor 2: `S.Set(path, value, instanceId)` hands it to `resolveRoot(parts, id)`. The host does not use it. `settings/Schema.lua`'s `resolveRoot` ignores the id (it always answers `NS.db.profile`), and the colon wrappers `NS.Schema:Set(path, value)` / `NS.Schema:Get(path)` do not forward one.

## Option (a): adopt instance addressing

1. **Resolver.** `resolveRoot(parts, id)` maps an instance id to its panel registry record (and keeps the profile root when no id is given).
2. **Rows.** Register instance-relative schema rows for every `C.PANEL_FIELD_TYPE` field (colors, border / bar / bar-border blocks, textures, size, `strata`, `level`, `scale`, `alpha`, mouseover, `enabled`, the `art*` fields, the anchor `point` / `relPoint` / `x` / `y`). `name` keeps routing to `R:Rename`.
3. **Writes.** `Registry:Set` routes through `NS.SchemaRuntime.Set(path, v, id)`, and the whole-record and bulk verbs (`R:Reset`, `R:CopyFrom`, `R:FitToArtwork`, `R:Recover`, `R:ResetPositions`, the unlock drag-stop through `:SetPosition`) become callers of the helper. The colon wrappers forward the id.
4. **Retire the row.** The `architecture-§5` row in Documented deviations retires in the same change.

This is a large change (the largest per-record migration in the collection) for fields the Registry already validates, logs and announces, which is why the row is kept for now.

title: Fade elements by their own range check, with an opacity slider per feature
summary: What Give the cast bars, target frames and pet frames their own out-of-range fade: - a range check driven by spells, not just UnitInRange 's fixed ~40 yards, so it follows the player's own reach (a healer's heal, an Evoker's Living Flame at ~25–30 yards, a resurrect for a dead member); - an out-of-range opacity slider per feature (Cast Bars, Target Frames, Pet Frames), in place of whatever the par…
full_description:
## What

Give the cast bars, target frames and pet frames their own out-of-range fade:

- a range check driven by spells, not just `UnitInRange`'s fixed ~40 yards, so it follows the player's own reach (a healer's heal, an Evoker's Living Flame at ~25–30 yards, a resurrect for a dead member);
- an **out-of-range opacity slider per feature** (Cast Bars, Target Frames, Pet Frames), in place of whatever the party frame happens to use.

## Why this is an issue, not a feature yet

Out-of-range fading shipped the other way round, as *Fade with party frames* (General → Party frames, `general.rangeFade`, `modules/RangeFade.lua`):

- **EllesmereUI** and **Blizzard raid-style**: each unit's elements copy the alpha of that member's party frame, by post-hooking the frame's own `SetAlpha` / `SetAlphaFromBoolean`. The copy is exact, EllesmereUI's own `oorAlpha` setting included.
- **Blizzard classic**: `PartyMemberFrame` never fades for range, so there is nothing to copy. There the module asks `UnitInRange` itself on `UNIT_IN_RANGE_UPDATE` and fades to 0.5, the value the raid-style frames use.

The request was to copy the party frame when possible and to file this as the follow-up. It would add:

- the per-feature sliders;
- spell-based ranges on every frame system, which matters most on the classic layout, where the fallback is the 40-yard check at a fixed 0.5.

## Notes for whoever picks it up

- `C_Spell.IsSpellInRange` answers plain booleans for a friendly unit-targeted spell. `UnitInRange` can answer a **secret** boolean in combat, so it only reaches the frame through `SetAlphaFromBoolean`. EllesmereUI's `UpdateButtonRange` (EllesmereUIRaidFrames.lua) is a worked example: a friendly spell per class, a rez spell for dead units, `UnitInRange` as the fallback.
- A per-feature alpha must still multiply with the element's own alpha (Master alpha, the combat reshuffle fade, the cast bar fade-out). The per-unit fade frames in `modules/RangeFade.lua` are the place for it. A per-feature fade needs one fade frame per unit **per feature** rather than per unit.
- Target frames: decide whether "range" means range to the party member (what ships) or to the member's *target*. A compound token like `party1target` is outside `UnitInRange`'s group-member domain and never gets `UNIT_IN_RANGE_UPDATE`.
